# Delta Battery makes Army history with first IBCS-Patriot enabled certification on peninsula

20 November 2026

## From Eighth Army Public Affairs Office

 CAMP HUMPHREYS, South Korea — Delta Battery, 6th Battalion, 52nd Air Defense Artillery Regiment, 35th Air Defense Artillery Brigade, made military history in the Republic of Korea by successfully completing certification on the Integrated Air and Missile Defense Battle Command System (IBCS), becoming the first operational Patriot battery in the U.S. Army to achieve this milestone.

content:
2026年香港海事周圆满落幕，出席人数创历史新高，艺术集装箱奖项获奖中国劳工公告栏
星期日, 22 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港及中国劳工新闻（英文）
2026年香港海事周圆满结束，出席人数创历史新高，艺术集装箱奖项获奖
香港海事周2026于11月21日以艺术集装箱绘画比赛及学员嘉许仪式结束。交通部长表示，参与人数可能达到 20,000 人，高于去年的 18,000 人。宣布了八项新举措，以提高港口的弹性和货物吞吐量。
2026年香港海事周于11月21日在香港海事博物馆举行联合颁奖典礼，其中包括「艺术货柜航行」绘画比赛及杰出海事甲板及轮机学员嘉许计划。运输及物流局局长在活动上发表主旨演讲。
国务卿在仪式上致辞时指出，为期7天的活动现已进入第十个年头，吸引了80多个组织举办了60多项活动。虽然参与人数仍在统计中，但他表示，初步估计出席人数可能会超过去年的 18,000 人，达到近 20,000 人。 “这次最后一天的活动特别有意义，”他补充道。
艺术容器大赛精选了初级组、二级组和公开组的获奖作品，与其他入围作品一起在博物馆的户外展览区展示。局长重点介绍了多项体现香港特色的设计，包括麻将牌、红白蓝袋子、传统街景、冰屋地砖、点心和海鲜等图案。一个集装箱将香港与多条航线连接起来，形成星空形象，局长形容这是“航海的浪漫”。
在海事周期间，今年的主题是通过伙伴港口建立信任并通过多元化增强港口的韧性，宣布了八项成果。局长表示，这些不仅仅是签署谅解备忘录，旨在“增加货运量、增加价值”，并加强香港全球航运、物流和航空供应链的协同效应。
出席典礼的嘉宾包括立法会议员兼人力资源发展委员会委员林明峰、香港海事及港务局人力资源发展委员会主席古威灵、海事处处长黄世发、香港海事博物馆主席宋泽明、学员嘉许计划工作小组主席索马桑达奈尔船长、东方海外货柜航运有限公司陈康妮及现代货箱码头有限公司辉耀明等。

HK Maritime Week 2026 concludes with record attendance, art container awards | China Labour Bulletin Board
Sunday, 22 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
HK Maritime Week 2026 concludes with record attendance, art container awards
Hong Kong's Maritime Week 2026 ended on 21 November with an art container painting competition and a cadet recognition ceremony. Transport Secretary said participation likely reached 20,000, up from 18,000 last year. Eight new initiatives were announced to boost port resilience and cargo throughput.
Hong Kong's Maritime Week 2026 concluded on 21 November with a joint award ceremony at the Hong Kong Maritime Museum, featuring the "Art Container Voyage" painting competition and the Outstanding Marine Deck and Engine Cadet Recognition Scheme. The Secretary for Transport and Logistics delivered the keynote speech at the event.
Speaking at the ceremony, the Secretary noted that the seven-day event, now in its tenth year, had drawn more than 80 organisations organising over 60 activities. While participation numbers were still being tallied, he said initial estimates suggested attendance had likely surpassed last year's 18,000 to reach nearly 20,000. "This final-day event is particularly meaningful," he added.
The art container competition featured winning entries from primary, secondary and open categories, displayed alongside other shortlisted works in an outdoor exhibition area at the museum. The Secretary highlighted several designs that captured Hong Kong's character, including patterns resembling mahjong tiles, red-white-blue bags, traditional street scenes, ice-house floor tiles, dim sum and seafood. One container linked Hong Kong with various shipping routes to form a starry sky image, which the Secretary described as evoking "the romance of navigation".
During Maritime Week, eight outcomes were announced under this year's theme of building trust through partner ports and enhancing port resilience through diversification. The Secretary said these went beyond signing memoranda of understanding, aiming to "increase cargo volume, increase value" and strengthen synergies across Hong Kong's global shipping, logistics and aviation supply chains.
The ceremony was attended by Legislative Council member and Human Resources Development Committee member Lam Ming-fung, Wellington Koo, chairman of the Hong Kong Maritime and Port Authority's Human Resources Development Committee, Maritime Department Director Wong Sai-fat, Hong Kong Maritime Museum chairman Richard Sung, Captain Somasundar Nair, chairman of the Cadet Recognition Scheme working group, Connie Chan of Orient Overseas Container Line and Frank Fai of Modern Terminals.

content:
從台灣的倉頡換成大陸的漢語拼音：電腦輸入法會影響下一代學習中文嗎？ - BBC News 中文
圖像加註文字，倉頡碼開發於台灣，卻在香港長期受到廣泛應用。
10月底，香港特區教育局公布小學創科課程草擬文件，提出小學二年級學生應該初步掌握以中國普通話為基礎的「漢語拼音輸入法」輸入中文，引起社會熱議。
過去，教育局沒有規定學校應該教哪一種輸入法，而倉頡及其簡化版速成一直是港人常用選擇。
這份建議的出現，正好發生在倉頡輸入法雛形誕生50週年之際。
從倉頡到漢語拼音輸入，表面是打字方式的選擇，背後卻涉及文化改變及語言系統轉換。自2008年開始，港府已積極推廣學校用普通話教授中國語文。在此背景下，引入漢語拼音輸入做法再次觸碰港人神經。
「你會思考（政策）是不是要再削弱廣東話在香港的地位、要把普通話再普及化等等。」儘管從小用漢語拼音打字，今年32歲的梁先生說，這是他看到新聞後的第一想法。
另外有反對聲音擔心，拼音輸入法會影響學童的認字能力，甚至改變用語思維。教育局後來解釋，學生在普通話堂已經學習漢語拼音，有初步語音基礎，認為採用拼音輸入是「學以致用、相輔相成」。
輸入法會影響下一代學習語言嗎？有學者向BBC中文指出，輸入法本質是一項工具，未必直接左右學童的語言能力。而比起輸入法本身，學童目前身處語言環境的改變更值得關注。
圖像來源，South China Morning Post via Getty Images
圖像加註文字，2008年開始，教育局推出「以普通話教授中國語文科」計劃，簡稱「普教中」。
這是教育局首次在課程文件中，明確提出學生應該掌握的中文輸入法。
台灣高雄市選戰：「知識藍」柯志恩對決「新潮流」賴瑞隆，國民黨有可能複製「韓流」嗎？
早在2000年，政府就小學生的中文輸入能力訂下學習目標。時任教育統籌局局長王永平表示，小一至小三學生要學習用手寫輸入；而小四至小六學生則用鍵盤輸入。
但當時政府強調，不會規定學校教哪一種輸入法，因為「輸入法只是一種工具」，重點是令學生學懂打字，運用電腦學習。
而據教育署資料顯示，當時大部分學校教速成，職場上則普遍用倉頡。
香港教育大學數學與資訊科技學系副教授黎耀志博士向BBC中文指出，倉頡在香港流行的原因很「直觀」：因為「沒有別的選擇」。
中文輸入法主要分字形和字音兩種：拆解文字的倉頡、速成屬前者，描述讀音的拼音則屬後者。與台灣和中國大陸使用注音符號和漢語拼音不同，粵語過去未有形成一套統一拼音系統。但倉頡輸入並不依賴讀音。
倉頡由台灣電腦科學家朱邦復發明，目的是讓漢字可以用英文鍵盤輸入電腦。他把漢字按部首、筆劃拆解成不同字根，再對應24個英文字母進行編碼。每個漢字最多可拆五個碼。
速成輸入法是倉頡的「簡化版」：輸入時只需要取首尾兩個碼，然後再選字。
圖像加註文字，1999年8月26日，朱邦復先生（左）探訪香港教育大學（時為香港教育學院），黎耀志（中）及其兒子與先生合影。
黎耀志說，倉頡不易上手，使用者要理解漢字的結構、記住獨有的拆碼規則，「比較難學」。但輸入法能否成為主流，除了易不易學，也與使用者習慣、技術發展等有關。
例如，倉頡雖在台灣發明，但台灣人從小開始學習注音符號，所以注音仍然是當地主流輸入法。中國大陸曾流行把漢字拆成筆劃的「五筆輸入法」，但因為拼音輸入法日益進步，聯想詞越來越準確和快速，五筆的使用率就逐漸下降。
至於香港，利用數字鍵輸入選字的「九方輸入法」一度流行，但隨着數字鍵盤式微、「九方」開始收費，使用人群便減少。對比之下，為了普及中文電腦，朱邦復於1982年主動放棄專利權，使倉頡成為電腦內置的標準輸入法之一。
除此之外，倉頡重碼率低，輸入效率高，也成為上班族的首選。
香港教育大學語言學及現代語言系助理教授劉擇明記得，自己大約在1995年開始用電腦，當時微軟視窗（Microsoft Windows）作業系統已預設有倉頡、大易、行列等輸入法。他每一種都試過，系統不同，速度有快有慢，但倉頡剛剛處在平衡：有學習門檻、要練習，但學習時間合理。
到1990年代中後期甚至千禧年代初，公司開始大量使用電腦，劉擇明記得當時香港「滿街都是倉頡班」。普羅大眾坐在課室裡硬背字碼，聽着老師在黑板前教拆字，「想練的人就保持用倉頡，很快放棄的那些人就由倉頡變做速成」。
圖像加註文字，中文輸入法主要分字形和字音兩種：拆解文字的倉頡速成屬前者，描述讀音的拼音則屬後者。
從「國安教育」到「愛國主義教育」，北京如何逐步改造香港人思想2024年10月1日
香港國安法5週年：你愛國嗎？國安教育工程下的師生和公眾怎麼看2025年6月30日
香港教育局指引學生以漢語拼音輸入中文，理由是能提高學習效率。
局方指，學生已經學習過漢字拼音，用拼音輸入法是「學與教效能」原則下的「最佳選擇」。但外界爭議，安排長遠會對學生學習中文造成影響。
今年29歲的梁景鴻或有切身體會。他在深圳出生，小學教授普通話，故自7歲開始使用漢語拼音輸入。2009年，他移居香港。在他印象中，小學電腦室配有手寫板，但沒有強制學生使用哪一種輸入法。
到了中學，身邊同學主要使用速成。梁景鴻坦言，由於使用漢語拼音輸入，自己曾被同學取笑是「大陸仔」，「你會介意的，但沒有辦法、改變不到」。
他試過學速成，但速度始終比不上漢語拼音。香港特區政府文書職系要求中文打字每分鐘達20字——用漢語拼音，梁景鴻每分鐘可以打到77個字，屬於水平之上。
不過長期使用，他確實感到在書寫方面有影響，「真的會容易忘記字怎麼寫」。「我不需要知道每一粒字是怎樣組成、怎樣的結構，我只需要輸入（字母），一個中文字出來大概是那個樣子的， 我就知道是那個字」。
這是外界對學生使用拼音輸入的其中一種擔憂：倉頡速成要求使用者充分了解漢字結構，字音輸入僅依賴讀音拼字，長遠下去會加劇執筆忘字的情況。
香港浸會大學中國語言文學系一級講師蕭欣浩向BBC中文表示，現在的輸入法已附帶詞語聯想功能，所以倉頡、速成使用者未必需要認識每個字詞，也可以完成輸入。
不過他同意，中小學生正值累積詞彙、建立漢字記憶的階段，使用拼音輸入法可能會影響他們對漢字的理解。「速成也要拆字，你會知道它（字部首）是草字頭、是木字，但拼音的話，你會讀就可以了。」
為了解決忘詞問題，梁景鴻曾在手機裡加入筆劃輸入法，但最終衡量下來，打字速度始終不夠拼音快。
「如果可以分程度的話，語音輸入法（很大機會）會忘字，普通話拼音可能在中間，如果是手寫輸入法就一定不會忘了。」梁景鴻形容。
劉擇明則認為，字形字音輸入法各有長處：字形輸入可以訓練使用者對漢字的部件意識，而字音則可訓練語音靈敏度，「如果我只用字形輸入法，也可以用了30年你都不會讀那個字。」
在他看來，要解決忘字或錯別字問題，不能單靠使用字形輸入法，更重要是在學科上加強學生漢字部件的意識。
圖像加註文字，有學者指中小學生正值累積詞彙、建立漢字記憶時期，使用拼音輸入法或會影響對漢字的理解。
不過，社會的憂慮並不限於學生書寫能力的變化，更要放在香港整體語言環境轉變中理解。
香港中小學一直設有普通話科。2008年開始，教育局再推出「以普通話教授中國語文科」計劃，簡稱「普教中」。學校可因應校情，自行決定實施模式。
根據香港語文教育及研究常務委員會2016年的統計，有71.7%小學全級或於部份班級推行「普教中」。此後「語常會」未有再發表相關研究。近年則有本地媒體自行統計，發現香港仍有44%小學推行「普教中」。
教育局局長蔡若蓮曾指，學好普通話有利融入中國發展大局、增強民族自豪感和自信。而為配合粵港澳大灣區發展，教育局有責任培養學生普通話能力。
雖然教育局重申「兩文三語」政策不變，但在「普教中」持續推行的背景下，學童學習使用漢語拼音輸入法，觸發大眾對港府「推普滅粵」的擔憂。
「你會思考（政策）是不是要再削弱廣東話在香港的地位、要把普通話再普及化等等。」梁先生說。
今年32歲的梁先生，中小學均就讀本地國際學校，中文課以普通話授課，日常主要用英文和朋友溝通。直到中三、四認識校外朋友後，他開始學習中文輸入法，「在電話和電腦的鍵盤清單，唯一認識的就是拼音。」
他曾嘗試學習倉頡速成，「上YouTube看教學，我明白它的基本邏輯，但怎樣拆成Keyboard的部份則不能理解」。對他來說，漢語拼音沒有學習門檻，「等於你識英文就打到英文」。
根據特區政府統計處《2021年人口普查主題性報告：兒童》，88.3%香港兒童以廣東話作為家中最常用的交談語言。有聲音擔心，學童用漢語拼音打字，需要在腦內先把粵語轉換成普通話，長久下去壓縮廣東話的使用。
不過，梁先生的經驗並非完全如此。他自小用粵語和英語思考，認為思考語言早已成形，漢語拼音輸入法是後天學習的工具，所以在輸入時並不存在要把粵語翻譯到普通話的過程。
梁景鴻也有同樣感受。他表示自己在打字時是用粵語去思考，只不過廣東話中有不少獨有的助語詞，使用漢語拼音輸入需要刻意背誦，例如「唔」是「WU」、「嘅」是「KAI」，「咁」是「GAN」。
但梁先生不確認，在小學階段使用漢語拼音輸入會否改變思維，「讓他們多了理由去用普通話思考？」
蕭欣浩則認為，學童單用漢語拼音輸入未必會使粵語退步，但從宏觀的環境來看，學童本身學習語言環境早已發生改變，更令人值得關注。
「中文用普通話教、詞彙用普通話讀、日常生活溝通用普通話，現在連打字都用普通話，這個連帶關係可能會加重減少粵語思考和運用的時間。」
蕭欣浩在大學講學，留意到不少學生使用語言的習慣深受社交媒體影響，「比如作文，很明顯（看到）全部作文有穿越、宮廷等等（元素）」。
年輕人日常使用的潮語，也越來越多普通話用詞。早前，有香港社交媒體內容創作者隨機街訪數位「00後」年輕人，了解時下流行的潮語，當中有受訪者回答「繃不住」、「那咋了」。影片令本地網民訝然，感嘆潮語已經變得「大陸化」。
「為什麼（他們）現在講的是普通話潮語呢？就是聽得多嘛。」蕭欣浩說。
從節省教學時間的現實層面而言，蕭欣浩理解教育局的考量。但在「普教中」的大環境下，他認為漢語拼音輸入可視為其中一個配套，「去加強普通話學習」。
在倉頡和漢語拼音的討論以外，有人提出第三個選項——粵語拼音（粵拼）。
劉擇明一直積極推廣粵拼，創立過網上中文粵語詞典《粵典》。他強調，香港社會以粵語為主，學生要表達自己，「用粵語一定是好一些」。
「如果母語可以用字音輸入法，就可以鞏固返每一顆字的音，」劉擇明說。
不過，目前粵拼未被納入正規課程。教育局曾表示，粵語拼音輸入法等標音系統「缺乏一致性」，師生不容易掌握和熟習。梁景鴻和梁先生也曾嘗試學粵拼，但因為網絡上有不同的拼音方案，難以作出選擇。
劉擇明解釋，經過數年的發展和整合，粵拼在系統、教材和工具上已經「準備就緒」，只等待官方去推廣，而現時香港已經有特殊學校使用粵拼教授中文。
面對教育局建議漢語拼音，劉擇明理解局方望降低學生學習門檻。但他指出，輸入法教學不只考驗學生，也考驗老師對普通話的熟悉程度。
在他看來，目前課綱只建議三節課，課時僅得105分鐘，學生未必能在短時間內掌握一套輸入法。但老師可以讓學生了解到，輸入法並非只有一種，「拼音也不只得普通話」。
圖像加註文字，根據香港政府統計處《2021年人口普查主題性報告：兒童》，88.3%兒童以廣東話作為家中最常用的交談語言。
1976年，朱邦復開發出「中文形意檢字法」，至1979年獲得當時台灣三軍大學校長，蔣介石養子蔣緯國將軍建議，更名「倉頡輸入法」。
1990年代末，互聯網應用開始興起，他創立網站，整合倉頡輸入法教材，又加入拆字動畫、互動測驗等元素。當時，朱邦復留意到這網站，專程飛來香港與黎耀志會面，二人之後共同建立「倉頡之友・香港」項目，推廣香港人使用倉頡輸入法。
不過黎耀志坦言，這些年已很少留意輸入法的變化。因為隨着科技發展，輸入法早已不是資訊科技科的討論重點，「大家都將好多精力集中早幾年的STEM（科學、技術、工程與數學）、STEAM（科學、科技、工程、藝術與數學），甚至現在可能每間學校都在講AI。」
面對使用者的流失和變化，黎耀志看得淡然，坦言不會感到可惜，「各適其適就是最好的結果」。
在大學教書的劉擇明也發現，現在不少學生不懂得打字，「以前就語音輸入，或者很痛苦地在keyboard找字母，螳螂拳那樣打字；現在有了（Chat）GPT就再衰一些，語音講個字，然後GPT生成文章。」
劉擇明覺得隨着時代發展，工具會慢慢轉變，「現在都沒人用打字機了，所以工具真的會被淘汰。」不過在他看來，即便現在多人用語音輸入，但效果未能達到完全準確，最後仍要靠使用者自行修正，所以輸入法短期內未必會被取代。
他重申，每種輸入法都是不同模態，就像不同樂器，有易有難。輸入法沒有高低之分、從倉頡轉用拼音也不能稱為「退步」。
劉擇明說，當打字不再是「揾食必備技能」，表面上是少了人懂得倉頡速成，但換個角度看，這些人其實是「找到自己的方法去打字」。
蕭欣浩也認同。在現在的環境下，大眾很易把對政治意見、對粵語和繁體字的情感，甚至言語間的隔閡混為一談。但說到底，輸入法本質是工具，它在不同的時代流行，也會有被淘汰的一日。

# 海军造船计划将需要大幅增加年度拨款：国会预算办公室

国会预算办公室发现，5 月份发布的海军造船计划平均每年造船拨款约为 538 亿美元，比过去五年增加了 41%。

作者：[Diana Stancy](https://breakingdefense.com/author/dstancy/)，发表于 2026 年 11 月 20 日下午 2:33

 未来企业号航空母舰 (CVN-80) 的船尾部分正在 HII 纽波特纽斯造船厂的干船坞内建造。 （贾斯汀·卡茨/突破防御）

华盛顿——根据国会预算办公室的一份新报告，与近年来平均造船拨款相比，海军 2027 年造船计划将需要大幅增加年度成本。

具体来说，美国国会预算办公室周四发布的报告称，海军 [5 月份发布的造船计划](https://brokingdefense.com/2026/04/omb-director-rebukes-shipbuilders-over-products-delays/) 平均每年成本约为 538 亿美元，与过去 5 年海军每年约 38​​1 亿美元的拨款相比，总计增加了 41%。
CBO 表示，这一估算考虑了核动力舰艇加油、采购二手海运舰等非战斗力舰艇等成本，但这些成本并未纳入海军 2027 年造船计划，尽管此类费用通常来自造船资金。因此，与海军的造船计划相比，这些因素使国会预算办公室对海军平均每年造船成本的估计增加了约 46 亿美元。总而言之，这标志着造船支出达到了前所未有的水平。

报告称：“海军2027年造船计划的成本不仅与最近的资金相比很高，而且按照历史标准来看也很高。” “在过去的十年里，造船资金达到了自 20 世纪 80 年代里根政府国防建设以来的最高水平。自 2016 年以来，立法者普遍每年平均多拨款 25 亿美元用于造船。

# Navy’s shipbuilding plan would require massive hike in annual appropriations: CBO

The Navy’s shipbuilding plan released in May would average out to an annual cost of roughly $53.8 billion in shipbuilding appropriations — a 41 percent increase from the last five years, the Congressional Budget Office found.

By [Diana Stancy](https://breakingdefense.com/author/dstancy/) on November 20, 2026 2:33 pm

 Part of the aft of the future USS Enterprise (CVN-80) being constructed inside the dry dock at HII’s Newport News Shipbuilding. (Justin Katz/Breaking Defense)

WASHINGTON — The Navy’s 2027 shipbuilding plan would require a massive hike in annual costs in comparison to the average shipbuilding appropriations in recent years, according to a new report from the Congressional Budget Office.

Specifically, the Navy’s [shipbuilding plan released in May](https://breakingdefense.com/2026/04/omb-director-rebukes-shipbuilders-over-production-delays/) would average out to an annual cost of roughly $53.8 billion — totaling a 41 percent increase from the roughly $38.1 billion the Navy has secured annually in appropriations during the last half decade, the CBO report released Thursday said.

This estimate factors in costs stemming from refueling nuclear-powered ships, and procuring non-battle force ships such as used sealift ships, among other things — costs that are not factored into the Navy’s 2027 shipbuilding plan, even though such expenses are typically derived from shipbuilding funding, CBO said. As a result, those factors increase the CBO’s estimate of the Navy’s average annual shipbuilding costs by roughly $4.6 billion in comparison to the Navy’s shipbuilding plan. Altogether, this marks an unprecedented level of spending for shipbuilding.

“The cost of the Navy’s 2027 shipbuilding plan is high not only compared with recent funding but also by historical standards,” the report said. “Over the past decade, funding for ship construction has reached its highest levels since the Reagan Administration’s defense buildup in the 1980s. Since 2016, lawmakers have generally appropriated an average of $2.5 billion more per year for shipbuilding than the President has requested, partly because of concerns that the fleet is too small to perform all its missions.”

Accounting for only purchasing new ships in the recent shipbuilding plan, CBO estimates those ships would rack up to $1.47 trillion in 2026 dollars over 30 years. That’s an increase from the Navy’s estimate of $1.23 trillion over 30 years, per the report. CBO attributed these differences in new ship construction estimates to differences in “assumptions about the design and capabilities of some future ships.” Additionally, CBO acknowledged that it employed different estimating methods and accounted for growth of labor and material costs differently than the Navy.

The Navy’s [shipbuilding plan and budget request](https://breakingdefense.com/2026/05/navy-pushes-congress-to-back-constructing-auxiliary-ships-overseas/) seeks a total of $65.8 billion for shipbuilding alone for FY27.To advance the Trump administration’s Golden Fleet initiative, it calls for expanding the Navy’s inventory to 450 ships, including battle force ships, auxiliary ships, and unmanned vessels, by 2031.

“The pace of shipbuilding would be fastest in the next 10 years, reflecting the service’s desire to increase the size of the fleet as quickly as feasible,” the CBO report said. “It would slow from the mid-2030s to the mid-2040s; then construction would ramp up again in the late 2040s and 2050s to replace smaller ships, with a service life of 20 to 25 years, purchased in the first decade of the plan.”

莫斯科对制裁的怀疑可以追溯到 2000 年代。在2003年至2009年的六方会谈期间，俄罗斯认为制裁应该说服朝鲜保持对话而不是惩罚它。 2009年4月平壤宣布退出六方会谈后，时任俄罗斯副外长阿列克谢·博罗达夫金声称，与加强制裁相比，与会者最好讨论如何恢复多边机制。
2010 年 5 月朝鲜进行第二次核试验后，联合国加强了制裁，俄罗斯常驻联合国代表强调，这些措施不应产生负面的人道主义后果，而且如果平壤遵循决议的建议，制裁措施可能会被撤销。
2010年代，随着俄美关系逐渐恶化，对朝鲜的制裁力度加大。中美关系以及西方国家对俄罗斯实施制裁。朝鲜的案件被用来挑战单边制裁和美国发起的联合国制裁的合法性，俄罗斯外交部和联合国代表开始将这些制裁定性为过度且对人道主义局势有害。
2017年，俄罗斯外交官辩称，制裁没有实现其安全目标，并导致朝鲜生活条件恶化。然而，在表达对制裁影响的担忧的同时，俄罗斯仍然投票支持实施制裁，这可能是权衡了中国对朝鲜的不满。
自2022年俄罗斯入侵乌克兰以来，与美国和欧洲国家的关系急剧恶化，并对俄罗斯实施单方面经济限制。此后，莫斯科加大力度抹黑西方制裁。
在否决将1718委员会专家小组任期延长至2024年的决议后，俄罗斯常驻联合国代表瓦西里·内本齐亚表示，近年来专家小组的工作已经沦落到迎合西方。内本齐亚声称，朝鲜的合法活动已成为华盛顿领导的联盟施压的目标。
鉴于朝鲜对中国的重要性，俄罗斯否决将1718委员会专家组任期延长至2024年的决议的决定很可能是与中国协调的

Credit: Russian Presidential Press and Information Services
In recent years, Moscow’s official stance on North Korea’s denuclearization and sanctions has shifted: Russian diplomats now say denuclearization has become an irrelevant term and sanctions have proved ineffective. Both issues became part of Russia’s broader criticism of the United States’ policy.
Moscow’s skepticism of sanctions dates back to the 2000s. During the Six-Party Talks in 2003-2009, Russia argued that sanctions should persuade North Korea to maintain dialogue rather than punish it. After Pyongyang announced its exit from the Six-Party Talks in April 2009, Russia’s then-Vice Foreign Minister Alexey Borodavkin claimed participants would be better off discussing how to resume the multilateral format than strengthening sanctions.
When United Nations sanctions were tightened following North Korea’s second nuclear test in May 2010, Russia’s permanent representatives to the U.N. highlighted that the measures should not have negative humanitarian consequences and could be reversed if Pyongyang followed the resolution’s recommendations.
The sanctions regime on North Korea intensified in the 2010s, coinciding with the gradual deterioration of Russia–U.S. relations and Western countries’ introduction of sanctions on Russia. North Korea’s case was utilized to challenge the legitimacy of unilateral sanctions and the U.S.-initiated U.N. sanctions, as Russia’s Foreign Ministry and U.N. representatives began framing them as excessive and harmful to the humanitarian situation.
In 2017, Russian diplomats argued that sanctions did not achieve their security goal and caused a deterioration of living conditions in North Korea. While voicing concerns about sanctions’ effects, however, Russia still voted for their introduction, likely weighing China’s frustration with North Korea.
Relations with the United States and European countries deteriorated sharply since Russia’s invasion of Ukraine in 2022, and unilateral economic restrictions on Russia were imposed. Since then, Moscow has stepped up efforts to discredit Western sanctions.
After vetoing the resolution extending the mandate of the 1718 Committee Panel of Experts in 2024, Russia’s Permanent Representative to the U.N. Vasily Nebenzya argued that the Panel of Experts’ work had been reduced to playing up to the West in recent years. Nebenzya claimed that North Korea’s legitimate activities had become a target of the Washington-led coalition’s pressure.
Given North Korea’s importance to China, Russia’s decision to veto the resolution extending the mandate of the 1718 Committee Panel of Experts in 2024 was likely coordinated with Chinese counterparts, rather than made unilaterally. Although the United States and its allies launched the Multilateral Sanctions Monitoring Team (MSMT) to compensate for the loss of the Panel of Experts, Russia has stressed its illegitimacy, as it had no U.N. mandate. In 2026, Nebenzya claimed that MSMT’s reports were mere fabrications and disinformation.
The shifts in Russia’s official discourse on North Korea’s nuclear program are even more profound, evolving from firm condemnation of Pyongyang’s nuclear ambitions to acknowledgment of its self-defense measures as fully legitimate. A distinction should be made between North Korea’s nuclear and missile programs: while Moscow used to oppose Pyongyang’s nuclear tests, it never portrayed North Korean missile development as a threat. Russia’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs issued protests each time North Korea conducted nuclear tests in 2006, 2009, 2013, 2016, and 2017. The statements consistently highlighted that these actions pose a serious threat to peace and security on the Korean Peninsula and across the Asia-Pacific region, with negative consequences for Pyongyang.
After signing the 2024 Comprehensive Strategic Partnership agreement, Russia’s official rhetoric on North Korea’s denuclearization changed. In September 2024, Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov stressed that it was a “closed issue” for Russia, highlighting that denuclearization had lost meaning given the intensifying South Korea-U.S. military alliance. Visiting North Korea in summer 2025, he stated that Russia respects Pyongyang’s actions and understands the reasons why it carries out its nuclear program. Lavrov explicitly cited the US and South Korea’s military exercises and the 2023 Washington Declaration that allowed Seoul to participate in information sharing and consultations regarding nuclear contingencies as an explanation for increasing tension on the Korean Peninsula.
Similarly, in November 2026, Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova argued that Russia sees North Korea’s efforts to boost its defense capabilities “as entirely legitimate and justified, fully consistent with the right of self-defense enshrined in the U.N. Charter.” While this tacit acknowledgment of Pyongyang’s nuclear program challenges the NPT and the IAEA’s authority, Moscow frames its stance and North Korea’s policies as legitimate by selectively applying existing norms and interpreting international law in its own way.
Russia’s evolving approach to Pyongyang’s nuclear program and related sanctions is just one episode of its broader attempts to contest existing norms and challenge the United States’ foreign policy. It is also an example of Moscow’s effort to question the rules-based order, which it sees as imposed by Western countries without consideration of the interests of the Global South.
This line of criticism goes back to the late 2010s. In 2017, Lavrov argued that the West tries to replace the rule of law in international affairs with a rules-based order, suggesting that the Western interpretation of international law does not equal the law itself. As ambiguities in international law continue to expand and the international system becomes more polarized, more cases like North Korea may arise, where existing norms are contested.

title: One data foundation and many application layers drive the Army’s NGC2 transformation
zh_title: 一个数据基础和多个应用层推动陆军 NGC2 转型
summary: 陆军的下一代指挥与控制 (NGC2) 工作基于一个简单的前提：陆军无法再承担无法相互通信、需要数年时间更新或在对手堵塞链接时失败的 C2 系统。从印太地区的行动来看，这些问题变得尤为明显。陆军的答案是建立一个共享数据基础，将应用程序置于顶层，取代现在服务于火力、防空和后勤的单独的、特定于平台的系统。每个部件都经过精心设计，可以在保持内部功能的同时进行更换
content:
陆军的下一代指挥与控制 (NGC2) 工作基于一个简单的前提：陆军无法再承担无法相互通信、需要数年时间更新或在对手堵塞链接时失败的 C2 系统。从印太地区的行动来看，这些问题变得尤为明显。

陆军的答案是建立一个共享数据基础，将应用程序置于顶层，取代现在服务于火力、防空和后勤的单独的、特定于平台的系统。每个部件都经过精心设计，可以在保持与其余部件的互操作性的同时进行更换。

[Lockheed Martin](https://bit.ly/4tglqLK) 项目、企业运营副总裁钱德拉·马歇尔 (Chandra Marshall) 表示，NGC2 的核心是“将范式转变为以任务为中心的运营”。她说，陆军希望建立一个具有通用应用程序和核心服务的可组合架构，从而能够集成新软件、武器和传感器，而无需返工并消除每个梯队的孤岛。

**惩罚瘦腿的威胁图**
这种转变的例子始于电磁频谱。新美国安全中心国防项目研究员乔什·沃林指出，俄罗斯军队在乌克兰干扰、干扰和跟踪电磁频谱发射。他说，美国还没有遇到过如此严重地针对该频谱的敌人，而且陆军部队之间的通信和数据链接面临的风险随着印太地区强大的对手而增加。

然后是地理。沃林说，无论是全球反恐战争，还是当前的伊朗战争，甚至乌克兰战争，都没有要求陆军连接可能相距数千英里的系统。商业基础设施可以填补一些空白，尽管依赖蜂窝网络会更加困难。卫星通信可以提供另一种连接方式。

带宽可能是更严格的限制。陆军、海军和空军都在追求分布式作战概念，该概念假设分散的部队将不断在节点之间传递数据以保持同步。由于少数地点的兵力集结减少，这些数据必须通过更有争议的路径传输到更远的地方。

速度增加了压力，在乌克兰，“我们可能会讨论从获取到为目标提供服务的几分钟时间，”沃林说。
这个问题也存在于个别作战职能内部。在防空方面，直到最近，爱国者和萨德才能够通过萨德雷达控制爱国者拦截机相互提示。沃林认为，如果每个系统单独作战，分层防御就无法发挥作用。他说，这“效率极低”，而且面对大量传入威胁，烟囱式单位可能根本无法足够快地共享信息来协调响应。

2026 年 5 月 4 日，在菲律宾拉瓦格市拉巴斯沙丘举行的 2026 年“肩并肩”演习中，多国合作伙伴在反登陆实弹演习后合影留念。（美国陆军中士杜克·爱德华兹摄）

**数据层是基础**

马歇尔解释说，NGC2 数据层摄取信息，并根据角色、访问级别和作战功能将其提供给任何应用程序或操作员。陆军制定规则，系统使用这些规则来确定谁需要给定的数据以及该数据应该在哪个级别的部队使用。

这是 NGC2 面临的一个关键挑战，因为防空、后勤和火力每一次运行

【原文 English Original】
The Army’s Next Generation Command and Control (NGC2) effort rests on a simple premise: the service can no longer afford C2 systems that can’t talk to one another, take years to update, or fail when an adversary jams a link. Those issues become particularly glaring when viewed in the light of operations across a theater as vast as the Indo-Pacific.

The Army’s answer is a shared data foundation with applications layered on top, replacing the separate, platform-specific systems that now serve fires, air defense, and logistics. Each piece is built so it can be swapped out while maintaining interoperability with the rest.

At its core, NGC2 is about “shifting the paradigm to a mission-centric operation,” said Chandra Marshall, vice president, programs, enterprise operations at [Lockheed Martin](https://bit.ly/4tglqLK). The Army wants a composable architecture with common applications and core services, she said, enabling integration of new software, weapons, and sensors without rework and knocking down silos at every echelon.

**A threat picture that punishes stovepipes**

The case for that shift starts with the electromagnetic spectrum. Josh Wallin, a defense program fellow at the Center for a New American Security, points to Ukraine, where Russian forces jam, interfere with, and track electromagnetic spectrum emissions. The US hasn’t faced an enemy that targets the spectrum so heavily, and the risk to communications and data links between Army forces grows against a capable adversary in the Indo-Pacific, he said.

Then there is geography. Neither the Global War on Terror, nor the current fight in Iran, nor even the war in Ukraine has required the Army to connect systems that might sit thousands of miles apart, Wallin said. Commercial infrastructure could fill some gaps, although relying on cellular networks would be more difficult. Satellite communications could offer another means of connectivity.

Bandwidth may prove the harder constraint. The Army, Navy, and Air Force are all pursuing distributed operating concepts, which assume scattered units will continually pass data among nodes to stay synchronized. With less massing of forces in a few locations, that data has to travel farther and over more contested paths.

Speed adds pressure, and in Ukraine, “we might be talking on the order of minutes from acquisition to servicing a target,” Wallin said.

The problem exists inside individual warfighting functions, too. For air defense, only recently have Patriot and THAAD been able to cue each other, with a THAAD radar controlling a Patriot interceptor. Layered defense can’t work if each system fights alone, Wallin argued. It’s “super inefficient,” he said, and against a large volume of incoming threats, stovepiped units may simply be unable to share information fast enough to coordinate a response.

Multinational partners pose for a photo after a counter-landing live-fire exercise as part of Exercise Balikatan 2026 at La Paz Sand Dunes, Laoag City, Philippines, May 4, 2026. (U.S. Army photo by Sgt. Duke Edwards)

**The data layer is the foundation**

The NGC2 data layer ingests information and makes it available to any application or operator according to role, access level, and warfighting function, Marshall explained. The Army sets the rules, and the system uses them to determine who needs a given piece of data and at what level of the force it should go.

This is a key challenge for NGC2 because air defense, logistics, and fires each run their own data and communications infrastructure. Centralizing data across them, according to Wallin, will give logisticians trying to sustain distributed forces visibility into ongoing operations, the threat picture, and intelligence feeds that once lived in separate systems.

Pooling the data is the first step. The next is drawing conclusions about how information across functions relate. The 25th Infantry Division in Hawaii has been the experimental unit charged with demonstrating the approach, with Lockheed Martin serving as the Full Stack Operational Implementation Lead.

During Lightning Surge 3 in April, the team fused sensors, fires systems, and airspace data into a single cloud-enabled picture, according to Marshall. She called it the first demonstration of cross-domain data sharing in the 25th ID environment, working across multiple locations that spanned Hawaii, the Philippines, and the broader Indo-Pacific. The outcome was a shared real-time view and compressed sensor-to-shooter timeline, she said.

The NGC2 program is also changing how the Army develops and fields C2 software. Rather than giving industry a fixed set of technical requirements, the Army established operational objectives that could be refined as soldiers used the systems. That has allowed developers to incorporate feedback directly from the field instead of waiting for the next major upgrade cycle.

“They give us feedback real time so we can make software changes within minutes, hours, days, depending on the complexity of the feature,” Marshall said. “When we conduct Lightning Surges, it’s about operational fight-tonight capability the 25th ID can use now. It’s not a prototype, so it’s been powerful in that regard.”

One example came during Lightning Surge 4, when soldiers wanted to operate the system without having to interact physically with a screen. Developers responded by integrating an AI-driven hand microphone with an Army edge device, allowing soldiers to issue spoken commands instead of touching. The capability was designed, built, and delivered within days, according to Marshall.

The approach represents a departure from programs in which requirements are established years before soldiers receive the resulting capabilities. Marshall said the team delivered NGC2 solutions in less than 10 months that the 25th ID used operationally across the Pacific and exercised during Balikatan, the annual US-Philippine military exercise.

**AI as an aid, not a decider**

Artificial intelligence (AI) is one of the applications layered on top of the data foundation, though both Marshall and Wallin were careful about how much weight to put on it. AI can comb through available data and turn it around to commanders quickly, cutting latency from minutes to seconds, according to Marshall. However, it is one tool among several, and it isn’t making decisions for the Army. It correlates data and offers recommendations so commanders have the right information at the right time. The decision aids already demonstrated are “very powerful,” she said.

The practical hope for AI, in Wallin’s view, is to automate what can be automated and speed up tasks that are heavily manual today. Even “a 60 percent solution on something that was 100 percent manual before” could free operators to focus on other responsibilities, he said.

Another important feature of NGC2 is that its architecture is designed so its layers can be pulled apart and replaced independently. The Army is trying to separate the physical data links, meaning which cable runs to which radio and which satellite, from the compute infrastructure, and to separate both from the software that manages the data, Wallin said. Soldiers interact with the application layers on top.

If an adversary finds a new way to jam or track something like a satellite terminal, the Army could replace that hardware with something less vulnerable without disturbing everything above it. Advances in computing power and the shrinking size of computing hardware could give the Army more room to accommodate future applications. More importantly, the service is moving away from the assumption that software and hardware acquired today must remain in service for decades.

The goal is to create an architecture that can continuously evolve as adversaries develop new methods of disrupting communications, targeting military networks, and exploiting vulnerabilities. Instead of replacing an entire C2 system, the Army could update individual components while preserving the larger data infrastructure.

**Building a C2 ecosystem that evolves**

Implementation of the Army’s Modular Open Systems Approach to NGC2 also makes it easier to move beyond specific suppliers and systems when they underperform or aren’t pacing evolving threats with improvements. At the 25th ID, Lockheed Martin runs what Marshall called a strict onboarding and offboarding process, evaluating each element with the Army to decide whether it is the right fit for its piece of the architecture.

That differs from traditional acquisition programs in which a single prime contractor may control much of the system and replacing a supplier can mean extensive integration work. By establishing common interfaces and services, the Army is attempting to make competition and continuous upgrades part of the architecture itself.

The ecosystem is already large. More than 60 companies have contributed to the Army’s NGC2 effort or are under analysis for it, Marshall said, including small businesses, nontraditional innovators, and commercial-technology providers. The 25th ID’s data platform is based on Raft’s Raft Data Platform. Amazon Web Services supplies Wickr Chat, a communications and collaboration tool. Rune Technologies delivered TyrOS for contested logistics.

For the Army, the larger test will be whether the approach demonstrated by the 25th ID can be extended to other formations without recreating the stovepipes NGC2 was designed to eliminate. The ongoing Lightning Surge exercises and the 4th Infantry Division’s Ivy Sting exercises at Fort Carson represent opportunities to evaluate how common data infrastructure, modular applications, and soldier-driven software development can support different operational requirements.

The stakes are particularly high in the Indo-Pacific, where formations will be separated by thousands of miles and forced to operate with intermittent comms. A shared architecture will not eliminate those constraints, but it could give commanders the ability to exploit available data, change communications equipment, and incorporate new capabilities without rebuilding the entire C2 network.

content:
这两艘30米长的快速攻击艇在英国建造，将携带先进的防空和导弹系统，帮助乌克兰海军保护黑海谷物走廊。英国首相办公室新闻稿 英国和挪威正在联合资助乌克兰两艘先进快速攻击艇，以增强乌克兰的防御并向俄罗斯施加进一步压力。在此之际，安迪·伯纳姆总理和挪威首相乔纳斯·斯托尔今天与盟友一起参加了自愿联盟会议，以加大对乌克兰的支持并加强其长期安全。这些新舰艇由英国和挪威联合资助，并在英国建造，拥有类似护卫舰的能力，将以低廉的价格为乌克兰海军提供敏捷、强大的进攻和防空能力。这些30m长的舰艇配备了先进的防空、导弹和自卫系统，将显着提高乌克兰的海军能力和生存能力。它们还将帮助保护黑海谷物走廊，支持对乌克兰经济和全球粮食安全至关重要的出口。安迪·伯纳姆总理表示：“该项目由挪威资助，在英国本土建造，为乌克兰提供改变游戏规则的能力，不仅将加强黑海防御，还将支持欧洲安全。
“稳定和安全的海上通道是全球贸易的动脉，俄罗斯在黑海持续的不分青红皂白的袭击不仅伤害了乌克兰和我们的欧洲盟友，也伤害了世界上最脆弱的国家。“我感到自豪的是，这些英国制造的船只在英国和挪威的支持下，将有助于阻止这种侵略，并为乌克兰提供至关重要的进攻和防空能力。该计划将由英国和挪威通过两国共同领导的海事能力联盟提供同等资助，并展示两国如何共同努力将对乌克兰的支持转化为实际的军事能力。在英国建造的船只将配备欧洲供应商提供的先进尖端系统，汇集了整个欧洲大陆的国防技术和工业专业知识。国防部长韦斯·斯特里廷说：“乌克兰是世界各地争取自由的前线。只要我们的乌克兰朋友勇敢抵抗普京的野蛮和非法入侵，英国将与他们站在一起。 “这些新型快速攻击艇将加强乌克兰在黑海的防御，帮助保护重要的贸易路线并阻止俄罗斯的侵略，这不仅对乌克兰，而且对整个北约的安全都至关重要。”除了当前的冲突之外，这些船只将成为乌克兰在黑海的长期海上安全和威慑不可分割的一部分。
除了英国和挪威加强乌克兰的海上防御之外，总理还宣布增加 1000 架远程攻击无人机，以加强乌克兰抵御俄罗斯对平民的无情攻击。此前，国防部长韦斯·斯特里廷周二在乌克兰国防联络小组上宣布了一项重大防空计划，并于上周实施了一系列严厉制裁，使英国成为第一个对所有十个国家实施制裁的国家。俄罗斯主要石油生产国。上个月，在预算中，首相和财政大臣还宣布为乌克兰提供超过 100 亿英镑的额外财政支持，同时英国也做出了长期承诺：

【原文 English Original】
Built in the UK, the two 30-meter Fast Attack Craft will carry advanced air defense and missile systems to help the Ukrainian Navy protect the Black Sea Grain Corridor. UK Prime Minister’s office press release Two advanced fast attack boats for Ukraine are being jointly funded by the UK and Norway to boost Ukrainian defence and apply further pressure on Russia. It comes as Prime Minister Andy Burnham and the Prime Minister of Norway, Jonas Støre, join allies today at a Coalition of the Willing meeting to step up support for Ukraine and strengthen its long-term security. Jointly funded by the UK and Norway, and built in the UK, the new vessels boast frigate-like capability and will provide the Ukrainian Navy with agile and powerful offensive and air defence capabilities at a fraction of the price. Equipped with advanced air defence, missile and self-defence systems, the 30m boats will significantly increase Ukraine’s naval capability and survivability.  They will also help protect the Black Sea Grain Corridor, supporting the exports that are critical to Ukraine’s economy and global food security.  Prime Minister Andy Burnham said:   “Funded with Norway, built here at home in the UK, and delivering game-changing capability to the Ukrainians, this project will not just strengthen Black Sea defences, but supports European security too. “Stable and secure sea lanes are arteries of global trade, and Russia’s ongoing indiscriminate attacks in the Black Sea are not just hurting Ukraine and our European Allies but also hitting the world’s most vulnerable. “I am proud that these British made vessels, backed by the UK and Norway, will help to deter that aggression and provide vital offensive and air defence capability to Ukraine.” The programme will be funded equally by the UK and Norway through the Maritime Capability Coalition, which the two countries jointly lead and demonstrates how the two nations are working together to turn their support for Ukraine into practical military capability. The boats which are built in Britain will be fitted with advanced cutting-edge systems that have been provided by European suppliers, bringing together defence technology and industrial expertise from across the continent.  Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said:  “Ukraine is the front line for freedom everywhere. The UK will stand with our Ukrainian friends for as long as it takes as they bravely resist Putin’s barbaric and illegal invasion.   “These new fast attack boats will strengthen Ukraine’s defences in the Black Sea, help protect vital trade routes and deter Russian aggression, which is critical to the security of not just Ukraine, but the whole of NATO.” Beyond the current conflict, the boats will form an integral part of Ukraine’s long-term maritime security and deterrence in the Black Sea.   In addition to the UK and Norway’s boost to Ukraine’s maritime defensives, the Prime Minister also announced 1000 more long range strike drones to reinforce Ukraine against Russia’s callous attacks on civilians. That followed a major package of air defence announced by Defence Secretary Wes Streeting at the Ukraine Defence Contact Group on Tuesday, and a sweeping set of stinging sanctions last week, making the UK the first country to sanction all ten of Russia’s major oil producers.  Last month, at the budget, the Prime Minister and Chancellor also announced more than £10 billion in additional financial support for Ukraine, alongside the UK’s enduring commitment of £3 billion a year in military assistance. -End- P-50U Fast Inshore Attack Craft (FIAC) displayed by Babcock during DSEI 2021. Note the 2×4 SSM launcher (likely Marte) and the stern launcher for Maritime Brimstone. Naval News comments: Notably, the UK government’s press release does not name the shipyard selected to build the two 30-meter vessels, nor does it identify the specific hull design. Prior to Russia’s full-scale invasion, London and Kyiv had pursued a much larger fast attack craft program under their October 2020 Memorandum of Intent and the February 2022 UK-Ukraine framework agreement . As Naval News previously reported when initial details emerged on the UK-built FACM vessels , that earlier plan envisioned eight 50-to-65-meter missile boats, centered on Babcock’s 50-meter P-50U Fast Inshore Attack Craft design unveiled at DSEI 2021, with the lead hulls built in Britain and the remainder in Ukraine. Shifting to two 30-meter boats represents a considerably more compact platform, leaving open whether Babcock has proposed a scaled-down design or whether another builder has been tapped, particularly as no UK naval shipyard has recent experience building a 30-meter fast attack craft of this type. Another intriguing possibility is OCEA. The shipbuilder already has direct operational experience supplying Ukraine, having won the contract for 20 32-meter FPB 98 MkI aluminum patrol boats for the State Border Guard Service of Ukraine, the first pairs of which were spotted transiting the Istanbul Strait aboard a cargo vessel in 2023 . Beyond patrol craft, OCEA maintains Fast Attack Craft Missile (FACM) designs in its portfolio, including a missile-armed variant (VFPB 98) pitched to the Philippine Navy. Crucially, following its 2022 merger with The Wight Shipyard Co., OCEA operates an aluminum shipbuilding facility in East Cowes on the Isle of Wight, giving it the domestic UK footprint needed to meet a “built in the UK” requirement. Nevertheless, because OCEA remains headquartered in Les Sables-d’Olonne and is widely perceived as a French shipyard, awarding it a flagship British-Norwegian-funded naval contract could carry political sensitivities in London. OCEA’s VFPB 98 (very fast patrol boat) scale model seemingly fitted with a MSI-DS Seahawk main gun, two Narwhal RWS and two Marte anti-ship missiles. These are 32 meters FACM and Ocea has a yard on the Isle of Wight, giving it the domestic UK footprint. Naval News picture by Aaron Matthew Lariosa. Finally, downsizing from the initial 50-meter Babcock P-50U design to a 30-meter hull carries a major logistical advantage for delivery: with the Turkish Straits closed to warships under the Montreux Convention, a more compact 30-meter vessel can likely reach the Black Sea via Europe’s inland waterways and the River Danube. summary: 英国陪审团发现，一名被指控为香港从事间谍活动的前英国海军陆战队员自杀身亡。马修·特里克特（Matthew Trickett）在一家公共服务公司未能找到他并安装他的电子标签后结束了自己的生命。马修·特里克特（Matthew Trickett）是被伦敦警方指控涉嫌为香港从事间谍活动的三名男子之一。照片：皇家海军陆战队。 2024 年 5 月，这位 37 岁的男子被发现死于梅登黑德的格伦费尔公园。几周前，他因涉嫌协助香港情报部门而根据英国国家安全法被捕并受到指控。 Trickett – 内政部移民办公室
content:
英国陪审团发现，一名被指控为香港从事间谍活动的前英国海军陆战队员自杀身亡。马修·特里克特（Matthew Trickett）在一家公共服务公司未能找到他并安装他的电子标签后结束了自己的生命。马修·特里克特（Matthew Trickett）是被伦敦警方指控涉嫌为香港从事间谍活动的三名男子之一。照片：皇家海军陆战队。 2024 年 5 月，这位 37 岁的男子被发现死于梅登黑德的格伦费尔公园。几周前，他因涉嫌协助香港情报部门而根据英国国家安全法被捕并受到指控。特里克特是内政部移民官员，在拘留期间被发现在牢房内试图自残，但两天后被保释。 💡 如果您需要支援，请致电：撒玛利亚会 2896 0000（24小时，多语种）、预防自杀中心 2382 0000 或政府心理健康热线 18111。香港辅导及心理学会提供中英文 WhatsApp 热线：6218 1084。另请参阅：HKFP 心理健康热线卫生服务指南。据英国广播公司报道，雷丁验尸官法院的陪审团周三发现，为英国政府提供司法和惩教服务的 Serco 多次“未能采取合理措施”找到他的地址。特里克特的同案被告卫彼得·韦(Peter Wai)和袁国强(Bill Yuen)因协助香港外国情报部门于6月分别被判入狱10年和8年。
前英国边防部队官员韦伟被判在香港驻伦敦经济贸易办事处办事处经理袁先生的命令下进行“影子警务”行动。左起：香港经济贸易办事处（香港经贸办）官员袁国强和前英国边防部队官员韦伟伟。照片：伦敦警察厅。这两名具有中英双重国籍的人针对的是居住在英国的香港民主抗议者。香港否认与明显的间谍活动有任何联系。全文：解释者：英国当局为何逮捕与香港驻伦敦经济贸易办事处（香港经济贸易办事处）有联系的 3 名男子。照片：维基共享资源。据称，这两人监视的人中有活动人士罗冠聪 (Nathan Law)，他被香港国安警察通缉，悬赏 100 万港元。由于担心“羞辱”，特里克特于 2024 年 5 月 23 日（即他应出庭的前一天）写了一封给家人的最后一封信。据报道，陪审团表示：“在得知警方试图找到他并担心他会被逮捕并重新拘留后，马特提前了他的计划，并将信函的日期重新调整为 5 月 19 日。”特里克特的一位朋友上周告诉法庭，特里克特自 2013 年以来一直担任私人安全顾问，他担心可能的定罪会带来“耻辱”，并警告他可能会自杀。马修·特里克特（Matthew Trickett）是被伦敦警方指控涉嫌为香港从事间谍活动的三名男子之一。
照片：LinkedIn via M.Trickett 高级验尸官 Heidi Connor 表示 Serco 尚未进行内部调查，并补充说该公司必须“改进其系统”以降低更多人死亡的风险。一个简单的谷歌地图搜索就可以避免她所说的“非常罕见”的情况。在周三的裁决之后，Serco 的发言人表示，该公司将审查验尸官的报告和建议。

【原文 English Original】
A former British marine who was charged with spying for Hong Kong died by suicide, a UK jury has found. Matthew Trickett took his own life after a public services firm failed to locate him and fit his electronic tag. Matthew Trickett, one of the three men charged by London police on suspicion of spying for Hong Kong. Photo: Royal Marines. In May 2024, the 37-year-old was found dead in Maidenhead’s Grenfell Park. He had been arrested and charged under the UK’s National Security Act weeks earlier for allegedly assisting Hong Kong’s intelligence service. Trickett – a Home Office immigration officer – was seen attempting self-harm in his cell while in detention, but was released on bail two days later. 💡 If you are in need of support , please call: The Samaritans 2896 0000 (24-hour, multilingual), Suicide Prevention Centre 2382 0000 or the gov’ t mental health hotline on 18111. The Hong Kong Society of Counselling and Psychology provides a WhatsApp hotline in English and Chinese: 6218 1084. See also: HKFP’s mental health services guide. On multiple occasions, Serco – which provides judicial and correctional services to the UK government – “failed to take reasonable steps” to locate his address, the jury at Reading Coroner’s Court found on Wednesday, according to the BBC. Peter Wai and Bill Yuen, Trickett’s co-defendants, were jailed for 10 and eight years, respectively, in June for assisting Hong Kong’s foreign intelligence service. Wai, a former UK Border Force officer, was convicted of conducting a “shadow policing” operation upon the orders of Yuen, an office manager at the Hong Kong Economic and Trade Office in London. From left: Hong Kong Economic Trade Office (HKETO) official Bill Yuen and former UK Border Force officer Peter Wai. Photos: Metropolitan Police. The two British-Chinese dual nationals targeted Hong Kong pro-democracy protesters living in the UK. Hong Kong denied any link to the apparent spying . In full: Explainer: Why UK authorities arrested 3 men linked to Hong Kong’s trade office The Hong Kong Economic and Trade Office (HKETO) in London. Photo: Wikimedia Commons. Among those the pair were said to have surveilled was activist Nathan Law, who is wanted by national security police in Hong Kong with a HK$1 million bounty on his head. Fear of ‘humiliation’ Trickett had penned a final letter to his family dated May 23, 2024 – the day before he was due to appear in court. “Upon learning that police were trying to locate him and fearing he would be arrested and taken back to custody, Matt brought his plan forward and re-dated his letter to May 19,” the jury reportedly said. One of his friends told the court last week that Trickett, who had worked as a private security consultant since 2013, feared the “humiliation” of a possible conviction and had warned he might kill himself. Matthew Trickett, one of the three men charged by London police on suspicion of spying for Hong Kong. Photo: LinkedIn via M. Trickett Senior coroner Heidi Connor said Serco had yet to carry out an internal investigation, adding that the company must “improve its systems” to mitigate the risk of more people dying. A simple Google Maps search could have averted what she nevertheless said was a “very rare” scenario. Following Wednesday’s ruling, a spokesperson for Serco said the company would review the coroner’s report and recommendation.

【原文 English Original】
Subscribe here: Apple Podcasts | Spotify | YouTube Beyond the salacious details of the Nvidia–Jensen Huang scandal is a story about national security and the advanced chips powering the AI boom. But what exactly are these chips, and why do they matter? Ben Buchanan was one of President Biden’s AI advisers and helped write some of the U.S. policies on chip controls, in conversation with people like Huang. In this episode of Galaxy Brain , he breaks down what makes those chips so valuable and why they have such implications for the U.S.-Chinese relationship and the future of AI. The following is a transcript of the episode: Ben Buchanan: We had a lot of conversations with Jensen and with Nvidia. You would think if that is your policy, you would not want to sell chips to China. I don’t get it. I think it’s incoherent for the reason you describe. To be clear about what I do believe, my view is: American companies in fact do have to slow down. And I support pacing the frontier. We haven’t talked about it, but you know, part two of the book is all about how we regulated the AI companies, and what more we need to do on the regulation side. That was sort of huge part of our policy. And my view is that, in fact, the way in which we can create the space for regulation—as far back as 2021, we believed—was to slow China down. And China’s absolute dependence on American computing power was a way for us to slow China down, to build a lead for the United States. And then to, if you’d like, spend that lead on safety, to when the technology got to a critical moment. Which is what we’re in right now. To regulate the companies pretty aggressively, if I had my way. To make sure this technology is safe before it’s rolled out. Without this argument of: Well, we’re in an arms race with China; we must forge ahead . Which I thought was just very destructive. Warzel: So where does this all leave us right now, as we’re sitting in the story here? We’re talking Wednesday, November 18th. Obviously, things are changing by the minute. Buchanan: Always good to timestamp these conversations, ’cause it’s been changing every 24 hours. Warzel: Genuinely, it is. How much hot water is Jensen in? How dangerous and serious is this for Nvidia, as Huang goes to testify before Congress in December? Like, what are the stakes for both Huang and Nvidia going forward? Buchanan: I think they’re very high. Congress, in a bipartisan way, said it’s gonna do an investigation here. I don’t know what’s gonna turn up, but certainly they’ve got a lot of threads to pull. Whether or not there’s a criminal investigation, I have no idea. But I do suspect there will be a lot of government investigations into what happened here, and there should be. I guess in the medium term, Nvidia’s chips are still gonna be really good, and there’s still gonna be big demand for them. So as long as Nvidia can keep making great products, I think they will continue to sell those products. I guess it’s an open question of: Can they make great products without Jensen? We’ll see. They’ve got 31,000 research engineers, or something like that. So there’s a lot of smart people there, and they’ve got a lot of great technology. So we’ll see what happens to them technologically. But yeah; in the context of the investigations, certainly I would describe this as a serious moment. Warzel: What should senators be asking? Or what should anyone in Congress be asking Huang when he’s up there, you know, in front of Congress? Buchanan: It’s the most important, age-old question in any kind of D.C. investigation, which is: What did you know, and when did you know it? And they should be asking Jensen that, and they should be asking the commerce secretary, Howard Lutnick, that. Who knew what about where these chips were going. Who was getting them. How active was Nvidia’s role in enabling smuggling? How active was Jensen’s role? Again, I don’t have firsthand knowledge of the answers. But those were all the questions I’d be asking. Warzel: And I think lastly here, what has this done for the AI ecosystem right now? Like, is it in a worse place than it was? Or let’s just say, the American AI ecosystem? Is it in a worse place than it was two weeks ago, before all of this stuff really trickled out into the press? Or it was about the same? Buchanan: I think it probably creates some turbulence in the waters, but my suspicion is we’ll look back at this in six or 12 months, and the big story of AI will be largely unchanged by this. And the big story of AI, you know—as we spent a lot of detail on the book—is: You have really powerful chips being used by really capable algorithms, at larger and larger scales. Yielding extraordinarily capable systems, with profound national-security implications and profound implications for everyday life and democratic values. That story. To be clear, I’m not a cheerleader for that story. You know, you don’t write a book called The Bitter Struggle if you’re a cheerleader. But I think that story is largely undiminished by these events here. Warzel: What about China? Where are they better off? Are they worse off than they were? Buchanan: They’re worse off. They’re absolutely worse off. Because there was a bipartisan consensus that was forming on denying China access to computing power. But they had big allies that were saying, You know, let’s sell China the chips . And those allies were having some success. Chief amongst some, Jensen. David Sacks, Trump’s—my successor, as you know—AI adviser to the president, was advocating for this, at least based on the reporting. President Trump had advocated for in some context. And now the bipartisan consensus has, at least so far, started to harden against them. That is bad for China’s access to compute, and ultimately that is bad for China. Warzel: Ben Buchanan: Thank you for coming and helping to demystify this; talking about it in these very plain terms. I wanna have you back on, to talk about the regulation part of this, later. But this has been very helpful. Buchanan: It is great to talk about this subject, and it’s great to have interest in this subject of the chips and chip controls. Because this is a wonky subject for sure—that now has gotten this gloss of a sex scandal and a spy story. But I don’t think it’s an exaggeration to say this is one of the most important subjects in the world for U.S. national policy. Warzel: And we’ll keep following it. Thank you very much, Ben, for coming on. Buchanan: Thanks for having me. [ Music ] Warzel: If you liked what you saw here, new episodes of Galaxy Brain drop every Friday. You can subscribe on The Atlantic ’s YouTube channel, or on Apple or Spotify, or wherever it is that you get your podcasts. And if you want to support this work, and the work of my fellow colleagues, you can subscribe to the publication at TheAtlantic.com/Listener. That’s TheAtlantic.com/Listener. Thanks so much, and I’ll see you on the internet. For much of the year, Letná Plain has nothing to offer either locals or tourists.  It’s a large, featureless patch of land opposite the Sparta Prague football stadium. The surface alternates between dust and mud; there’s a car park for buses, and sometimes a circus. But every so often, Letná hosts an event that can tilt the world of Czech politics on its axis. Sometimes a little. Sometimes a lot.  On Saturday, November 25, 1989, around 750,000 people gathered to demand the end of Czechoslovakia’s communist regime. The following day, many returned, and on Wednesday, November 29, parliament abolished the Communist Party’s leading role in society. Nothing like that is going to happen this time around, but on Sunday, November 15, there were perhaps 400,000 people on Letná for the largest demonstration in Prague since the Velvet Revolution. It looked huge when viewed from a media platform overlooking an ocean of flags and faces.   The people who had gathered in the tens of thousands were there to protest against government plans to scrap the $10 monthly license fee which funds the nation’s two public broadcasters, Czech TV and Czech Radio. This may not seem an outrageous proposal, but to many Czechs it deepens their distrust of their billionaire Prime Minister Andrej Babiš and his populist coalition.   The premier, who has spent years in court fighting EU subsidy fraud allegations , is no fan of public broadcasting.  Get the Latest Sign up to receive regular emails and stay informed about CEPA's work. In 2017, Babiš, who was then finance minister, described Czech TV’s investigative reporters as “a corrupt rabble making reports to order.” In 2024, he said public broadcasters were part of the then governing coalition’s “media division.”  But it is his coalition ally, the far-right SPD party, that has spearheaded the campaign to scrap the license fees and replace them with direct state funding. The fear is that state funds will come with strings pulled by politicians. Tokyo-born businessman Tomio Okamura, the SPD chairman and now parliament’s speaker, has said he would vote for a bill to abolish the broadcasters altogether if someone submitted one.  The third coalition partner is the MAGA-friendly Motorists for Themselves party, which was against scrapping the fees but is now in favor. One Motorist MP said public broadcasting had been turned into a totem by one half of Czech society, which was giving the other half the finger.  What is clear is that the government has not covered itself in glory. After months of vague and occasionally rancorous debate, and just days after all three coalition parties did poorly in Senate and local elections, the first reading of the bill was rushed through parliament in the middle of the night, with a vote scheduled for 4:36 am on Saturday, October 24. The bill envisages a cut in funding of around 15%, reversing an increase introduced by the previous government. Babiš is also floating alternative funding mechanisms, including voluntary contributions, and insists the government will not interfere in editorial decisions.  But there is a glaring contradiction. His government’s own impact assessment identifies the license fee as the funding mechanism that carries the smallest risk to the broadcasters’ independence. Direct state funding, it says, carries the greatest risk.  There has been much talk of “the Nordic model,” without acknowledging that there is no single Nordic model. Finland and Sweden, for example, have dedicated levies collected through the tax system, but Babiš has ruled out a new tax.  Observers are more worried about “the Slovak model.” There, the license fee was abolished in 2023 with a solemn promise to ringfence funding for Slovak Radio and TV and preserve its independence.  The following year, the broadcaster was dissolved by Robert Fico’s populist nationalist government and replaced. Critics say its successor is now toeing the government line. Babiš said he would not be deterred by mass demonstrations, though there was a tiny wobble from Culture Minister Oto Klempíř, who said after talks with Michael McGrath, the European Commissioner for Democracy and Justice, that he wanted to delay further debate on the bill until parliament had begun discussing legislation to implement the European Media Freedom Act.  The 72-year-old prime minister is in a tough spot. He seems tired and barely invested in the issue while his far-right coalition partner insists the fee has to go. Babiš is known to dislike big demonstrations, and the opposition senses an opportunity.  Following Klempíř’s suggestion to kick the issue into the long grass would be a logical course of action for the prime minister, but it may not be one that’s open to him.  Rob Cameron is a Prague-based journalist and broadcaster, and author of https://www.basedinbohemia.com/ where he writes about Central Europe through reporting, analysis and long-form storytelling. He spent 22 years as the BBC’s correspondent in the Czech Republic and Slovakia, covering politics, business, culture and major breaking news across radio, television and online. title: Ground View Pakistan: The smelter before the mine
zh_title: 巴基斯坦地面景观：矿井前的冶炼厂
summary: 在全球精炼能力已经超过现有精矿供应的情况下，巴基斯坦建立国内铜加工业的雄心可能会让冶炼厂领先于矿山。总理谢巴兹·谢里夫在伊斯兰堡举行的巴基斯坦矿产投资论坛 (PMIF) 上强调了这一雄心，承诺结束未加工矿物的出口，并呼吁西南部的雷科迪克项目和其他项目支持炼油厂、冶炼厂以及生产电缆和导体的工厂。 “在巴基斯坦开采，在巴基斯坦加工，在巴基斯坦制造，然后出口到世界其他地区
content:
在全球精炼能力已经超过现有精矿供应的情况下，巴基斯坦建立国内铜加工业的雄心可能会让冶炼厂领先于矿山。总理谢巴兹·谢里夫在伊斯兰堡举行的巴基斯坦矿产投资论坛 (PMIF) 上强调了这一雄心，承诺结束未加工矿物的出口，并呼吁西南部的雷科迪克项目和其他项目支持炼油厂、冶炼厂以及生产电缆和导体的工厂。谢里夫说：“在巴基斯坦开采，在巴基斯坦加工，在巴基斯坦制造，然后出口到世界其他地区。”这一举措反映出巴基斯坦希望从矿产财富中获取更多就业机会、技能和出口收入。但由于只有山达克 (Saindak) 一家铜矿生产厂，其旗舰 Reko Diq 项目仍在等待商业生产，该国面临着更紧迫的挑战：在投入数十亿美元建设加工基础设施之前建立可靠的矿山产出。巴基斯坦联邦规划、发展和特别倡议部长阿赫桑·伊克巴尔表示，政府现在要求投资者提交完整的价值链提案，而不是仅仅关注开采和原材料出口的计划。这一要求给探险家带来了特殊的挑战。铜冶炼厂是围绕特定精矿设计的，包括其品位、杂质和预期产量。
如果没有明确的矿产资源和可靠的生产，开发商就无法做出贷款人要求的原料承诺。Milbank 律师事务所能源和基础设施合伙人穆尼布·侯赛因 (Munib Hussain) 表示，合同原料是此类项目融资的主要要求之一。区别很重要。 2025 年 4 月，我认为仅靠采矿并不能实现关键的矿产独立性，因此应优先考虑对加工的投资。这一论点涉及美国，美国现有的矿藏和数十年的生产为下游投资奠定了基础。巴基斯坦正处于早期阶段，全球铜市场呈现出不同的经济现实。冶炼经济 随着中国的新设施与印度、中亚和非洲不断扩大的业务展开竞争，铜冶炼厂正面临产能过剩的困境。处理和精炼费用方面的压力显而易见，矿工向冶炼厂支付费用，将精矿转化为精炼金属。安托法加斯塔和中国冶炼厂同意 2026 年基准为每吨 0 美元和每磅 0 美分，低于 2025 年每吨 21.25 美元和前一年的 80 美元。现货费用已降至零以下，标准普尔全球普氏能源资讯 (S&P Global Platts) 1 月份的评估值为每吨负 47.40 美元。这些负费用意味着加工商实际上正在向矿工支付费用以确保精矿。
Wood Mackenzie 副总裁兼金属和采矿咨询主管帕特里克·巴恩斯 (Patrick Barnes) 在论坛上表示：“现在是建设冶炼厂的非常艰难的时期。”印度说明了其中的商业风险。阿达尼 (Adani) 价值 12 亿美元的卡奇铜冶炼厂每年需要约 160 万吨精矿才能满负荷运营。彭博社报道的进口记录显示，该公司在 2024 年 2 月至 2026 年 2 月期间获得了所需原料的四分之一以上。有关高杂质精矿相关运营不稳定的报道加剧了人们的担忧，尽管阿达尼对这些说法提出了异议。在其他地方，嘉能可关闭了位于菲尔州的帕萨尔冶炼厂

【原文 English Original】
Pakistan’s ambition to build a domestic copper processing industry risks putting smelters ahead of mines at a time when global refining capacity already exceeds available concentrate supplies.  Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif reinforced that ambition at the Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum (PMIF) in Islamabad, pledging to end exports of unprocessed minerals and calling for Reko Diq and other projects in the southwest to support refineries, smelters and factories producing cables and conductors.  “Mine in Pakistan, process in Pakistan, manufacture in Pakistan and then export to the rest of the world,” Sharif said.  The push reflects a desire to capture more jobs, skills and export revenue from Pakistan’s mineral wealth. But with only one producing copper operation, at Saindak, and its flagship Reko Diq project still awaiting commercial production, the country faces a more immediate challenge: establishing reliable mine output before committing billions to processing infrastructure.  Ahsan Iqbal, Pakistan’s federal minister of planning, development and special initiatives, said the government now asks investors to submit complete value-chain proposals rather than plans focused solely on extraction and raw-material exports.  That requirement creates a particular challenge for explorers. Copper smelters are designed around specific concentrates, including their grades, impurities and expected volumes. Without defined mineral resources and dependable production, developers cannot establish the feedstock commitments lenders require.  Munib Hussain, an energy and infrastructure partner at law firm Milbank, said contracted feedstock ranks among the principal requirements for financing such projects.  The distinction is important. In April 2025, I argued that mining alone would not deliver critical minerals independence and that investment in processing should take priority.  That argument concerned the United States, where established mineral deposits and decades of production provided a foundation for downstream investment. Pakistan is at an earlier stage, and the global copper market presents a different economic reality.  Smelting economics  Copper smelters are struggling with excess capacity as new facilities in China compete with expanding operations in India, Central Asia and Africa.  The pressure is evident in treatment and refining charges, which miners pay smelters to convert concentrate into refined metal.  Antofagasta and Chinese smelters agreed to a 2026 benchmark of $0 per tonne and zero cents per pound, down from $21.25 per tonne in 2025 and $80 the previous year. Spot charges have fallen below zero, with S&P Global Platts assessing them at minus $47.40 per tonne in January.  Those negative charges mean processors are effectively paying miners to secure concentrate.  “It’s a very tough time to build a smelter,” Patrick Barnes, vice-president and head of metals and mining consulting at Wood Mackenzie, said at the forum.  India illustrates the commercial risks. Adani’s $1.2-billion Kutch Copper smelter requires approximately 1.6 million tonnes of concentrate annually to operate at full capacity. Import records reported by Bloomberg indicate it secured just over a quarter of its required feedstock between February 2024 and February 2026.  Reports of operating instability linked to high-impurity concentrate have added to concerns, although Adani has disputed those accounts.  Elsewhere, Glencore has closed its Pasar smelter in the Philippines, while Australia has intervened to support the Mount Isa smelter in Queensland.  Even countries that have developed mines before building processing facilities remain exposed to supply disruptions.  Indonesia delayed its copper concentrate export restrictions until production at Grasberg, one of the world’s largest copper mines, could adequately supply domestic smelters. Freeport also had to demonstrate that sufficient concentrate had been reserved for its Manyar facility.  But a September 2025 mud rush at Grasberg forced Freeport to declare force majeure, leaving Indonesian processors short of material.  For Pakistan, these examples strengthen the commercial case for Reko Diq’s existing development plan.  The project is designed to export copper concentrate by rail to Port Qasim for shipment through the Pakistan International Bulk Terminal. Although that approach falls short of the government’s downstream ambitions, it positions Pakistan to benefit from the current shortage of concentrate rather than compete in an oversupplied smelting market.  Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb said Reko Diq’s first year of commercial production had been expected to generate $2.8 billion in exports, equivalent to roughly 10% of Pakistan’s current goods exports.  For an economy repeatedly constrained by balance-of-payments crises, that potential foreign exchange revenue is significant.  The opportunity also extends to Western supply chains. American and allied processors need dependable mineral supplies, making Pakistan’s emerging mining industry potentially more valuable as a concentrate exporter than as another entrant into copper smelting.  Domestic processing could still make economic sense for smaller, specialized operations targeting minerals with genuine refining bottlenecks and committed buyers. Antimony is one example, with at least one Pakistani processor pursuing refining capacity linked to prospective US offtake.  Exploration incentives  Pakistan’s taxation policies present another obstacle to establishing the mining industry needed to support future processing.  Waleed Ahmed Vohra, founder and chief executive of Pakistani explorer Ark Metals, said customs duties and taxes consume close to 30% of his exploration budget because the emerging industry depends heavily on imported equipment and foreign technical services.  “I really feel bad when I have to raise a hundred dollars and give 30 dollars to the government,” Vohra said.  Rather than seeking permanent exemptions, he proposes deferring those obligations until commercial production begins, allowing companies to invest more capital in exploration while preserving the government’s eventual tax revenue.  “Defer now to prosper tomorrow,” he said.  Aurangzeb acknowledged the industry’s concerns and said the government would consider changes to taxation and other policies, particularly measures supporting exporters. He pointed to the removal of super taxes in this year’s budget.  But he also emphasized Pakistan’s limited fiscal flexibility, warning that a tax-to-GDP ratio below 10% would be unsustainable. The country has only recently moved into double digits.  That creates a policy dilemma. Export-oriented tax relief provides little immediate benefit to explorers that may spend years defining deposits before generating revenue.  Deferral could bridge that gap without permanently eliminating government receipts, although it would postpone collections and leave the treasury exposed if projects never reach production.  Current incentives nevertheless favour processing.  At the forum, Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif announced the province’s first dedicated mineral processing zone at an industrial estate in Khushab, offering industrial land at nominal rent for 15 years alongside customs duty concessions.  Federal relief for explorers, including a reported 30-year sales tax exemption covering exploration and development, remains under consideration.  The contrast is striking: processing investors are receiving concrete incentives while explorers are still seeking comparable support.  Government officials appear increasingly aware of the sequencing challenge. Barnes said discussions at the forum showed that policymakers had carefully examined the conditions necessary to make domestic smelting commercially viable.  “They understand that until there’s a mining industry here, smelting is not really on the table,” he said. “If they get two, three, four mines that are producing, options start to open up for them.”  Pakistan does not need to abandon its processing ambitions. It needs to distinguish between commodities where domestic refining addresses a genuine supply-chain shortage and copper, where existing smelters are already competing for scarce material.  The immediate priority is to make exploration more attractive, establish dependable production and build an export industry capable of financing future downstream investment.  A domestic copper smelter may eventually make sense. Its economic justification will be stronger once Pakistan has several producing mines and the concentrate supply to sustain it.  For now, the furnace can wait for the rock.  * Erik Groves is a contributing analyst for MINING.COM and Corporate Strategy and In-House Counsel at Morgan Companies. He will attend and provide coverage of the Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum (PMIF) in Islamabad on November 12 and 13.
