AIA Hong Kong & Macau launches Omni Healthcare Circle to tackle rising costs | China Labour Bulletin Board
Sunday, 22 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
AIA Hong Kong & Macau launches Omni Healthcare Circle to tackle rising costs
AIA Hong Kong & Macau launched the Omni Healthcare Circle at its Healthcare Financing Summit 2026, a partnership model with private providers to improve care quality and sustainability. The initiative addresses a 60 per cent rise in private medical insurance spending from 2019 to 2023 and a 68 per c
AIA Hong Kong & Macau hosted its Healthcare Financing Summit 2026 on 21 November, bringing together government officials, regulators, healthcare providers, academics, financial planners and industry stakeholders to advance cross-sector collaboration. At the event, the insurer unveiled the Omni Healthcare Circle, a new partnership model with private healthcare providers designed to improve care quality, encourage appropriate and efficient use of medical resources, and support the long-term sustainability of Hong Kong's healthcare system.
Speakers at the summit included Secretary for Health Lo Chung-mau, Insurance Authority Chief Executive Officer Clement Cheung Wan-ching, and Permanent Secretary for Health Thomas Chan, who shared views on the future direction of Hong Kong's healthcare ecosystem. AIA Group Chief Executive and President Lee Yuan Siong also addressed attendees, reaffirming the group's commitment to supporting the sustainable development of healthcare in the city.
The gathering comes amid mounting pressure on healthcare financing in Hong Kong. Research commissioned by the Hong Kong Federation of Insurers and conducted by the Centre for Ageing and Healthcare Management Research at PolyU CPCE found that private medical insurance spending rose by more than 60 per cent between 2019 and 2023, while inpatient claim frequency climbed by 68 per cent over the same period.
AIA Hong Kong & Macau Chief Executive Officer Alger Fung noted that insurers, healthcare providers and other stakeholders each play a vital role in keeping quality healthcare accessible and affordable as life expectancy rises and medical needs evolve. He added that the summit aims to unite different parts of the ecosystem around shared challenges and drive meaningful progress through closer provider collaboration and healthcare financing innovation.
The Omni Healthcare Circle pairs clinical expertise with insights into healthcare utilisation and patient journeys to help patients navigate treatment paths and anticipate costs more clearly. The initiative focuses on three core areas: broadening access to high-quality and appropriate care by connecting patients with evidence-based care pathways aligned with clinical guidelines from the Institute for Medical Advancement and Clinical Excellence and recognised international standards; giving patients greater transparency and confidence through clearer, more objective information on care quality, outcomes and efficiency; and supporting timely treatment and a smoother experience by bringing providers and AIA together earlier in the patient journey to provide greater certainty around treatment plans and expected expenses while streamlining administrative processes.
CUHK Medical Centre and Gleneagles Hospital Hong Kong are the first private healthcare institutions exploring the model with AIA, with the insurer remaining open to partnering with additional like-minded private providers in the future. Alice Liang, Chief Proposition and Healthcare Officer at AIA Hong Kong & Macau, explained that the initiative translates collaboration into practical action. She noted that both hospitals have strong ties to leading Hong Kong universities, bringing strengths in clinical care, research and innovative medical technologies that help use medical resources more efficiently while extending benefits to patients and the wider community. The summit also featured panel discussions in which leaders from healthcare, insurance and related fields exchanged views on applying the Omni Healthcare Circle model to foster greater transparency and more predictable patient journeys.

Sunday, 22 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Police seek public help to find missing 72-year-old woman in Tai Po
Hong Kong police are appealing for information to locate a 72-year-old woman who went missing in Tai Po. So Suk-chun was last seen on Yuen Shun Road early on 20 November.
21 Nov 2026 at 17:02 HKT · updated 22 Nov, 04:24 · 1 min read
Hong Kong police are appealing for public assistance to locate a 72-year-old woman who went missing in Tai Po. So Suk-chun was last seen on Yuen Shun Road in the early hours of 20 November, and her family reported her missing to police on the same day.
The missing woman is described as about 1.6 metres tall, weighing approximately 55 kilogrammes, with a medium build, a round face, yellow skin and short black hair. She was last seen wearing a black jacket, black trousers and black-and-white sports shoes.
Police have urged anyone with information about the missing woman or who may have seen her to contact the Regional Missing Person Unit of the New Territories North at 3661 3113 or via email at [email protected]. Members of the public can also approach any police station with relevant information.

summary: 香港政策负责人概述特区在“一国两制”全球倡议中的作用中国劳工公告牌 星期日, 2026 年 11 月 22 日 · 香港 香港和中国劳工英文新闻 香港政策负责人概述特区在“一国两制”全球倡议中的作用 香港特别行政区行政长官政策组负责人在 11 月 21 日的论坛上表示，香港可以利用其“一国两制”优势，列举绿色债券、毒品监管、人工智能治理和国际争端解决机制，帮助推进中国的四大全球倡议钍
content:
香港政策负责人概述特区在“一国两制”全球倡议中的作用中国劳工公告栏
星期日, 22 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港及中国劳工新闻（英文）
香港政策负责人概述特区在“一国两制”全球倡议中的作用
香港特别行政区行政长官政策组负责人在11月21日的论坛上表示，香港可以利用“一国两制”优势，包括绿色债券、药品监管、人工智能治理和国际争端解决机制等，帮助推进中国的四大全球倡议。
香港特别行政区行政长官政策组负责人表示，香港可以在“一国两制”原则下发挥自身优势，为国家四大全球倡议作出贡献。 11月21日，在“中国香港专题论坛：新时代港澳管治​​与发展”上，这位官员概述了香港如何帮助落实全球发展倡议、全球安全倡议、全球文明倡议和全球治理倡议。
这位官员提到，在全球发展倡议下，财政部今年5月在香港发行了人民币计价的绿色主权债券，将中国的绿色融资安排与国际投资者联系起来。这位官员还提到了香港从三月份开始实施的新药品“一级审查”制度，以及计划中的药品监管中心，该中心旨在与国际标准保持一致并支持全球卫生界。
在全球安全倡议中，该官员强调了香港金融管理局的生成式人工智能沙箱，该沙箱允许金融机构在受控环境中测试技术和风险管理措施。这位官员指出，习近平主席在7月的世界人工智能大会上呼吁人工智能又快又稳，加强治理规则和技术标准协调。
在全球文明倡议下，该官员指出西九文化区的两个博物馆是文化交流的例子。香港故宫文化博物馆去年与多哈伊斯兰艺术博物馆合作，下个月将与巴黎吉美国家亚洲艺术博物馆合作。 M+最近与巴黎蓬皮杜中心和纽约现代艺术博物馆结成文化联盟。
对于全球治理倡议，这位官员强调了国际争端解决组织（IDRO），该组织在中央政府的支持下在香港设立了总部。 IDRO于5月记录了首个成功案例，即通过调解解决跨境海事争端。总部由旧湾仔警署改建而成，象征有分歧的各方如何通过调解找到多元化的解决方案。
这位官员表示，这些例子表明香港如何发挥自身优势，为国际合作做出贡献。这位官员还指出，在中央政府港澳事务办公室的支持下，今年7月成立的中国社会科学院港澳研究中心正在致力于构建“一国两制”的理论框架和学术话语。展望香港回归祖国30周年

Hong Kong policy chief outlines SAR role in global initiatives under 'one country, two systems' | China Labour Bulletin Board
Sunday, 22 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Hong Kong policy chief outlines SAR role in global initiatives under 'one country, two systems'
The head of the Hong Kong SAR Chief Executive's Policy Unit said at a forum on 21 November that Hong Kong can help advance China's four major global initiatives by leveraging its 'one country, two systems' advantages, citing green bonds, drug regulation, AI governance and the International Dispute R
The head of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Chief Executive's Policy Unit said Hong Kong can contribute to the nation's four major global initiatives by leveraging its advantages under the 'one country, two systems' principle. Speaking at the 'China Hong Kong Thematic Forum: Governance and Development of Hong Kong and Macao in the New Era' on 21 November, the official outlined how the city can help implement the Global Development Initiative, Global Security Initiative, Global Civilisation Initiative and Global Governance Initiative.
Under the Global Development Initiative, the official cited the Ministry of Finance's issuance of renminbi-denominated green sovereign bonds in Hong Kong in May this year, which connects China's green financing arrangements with international investors. The official also mentioned Hong Kong's new 'first-tier review' system for pharmaceuticals, implemented from March, and the planned drug regulatory centre, which aims to align with international standards and support the global health community.
On the Global Security Initiative, the official highlighted the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's generative artificial intelligence sandbox, which allows financial institutions to test technology and risk management measures in a controlled environment. The official noted President Xi Jinping's call at the World AI Conference in July for AI to be both fast and stable, and for enhanced coordination of governance rules and technical standards.
Under the Global Civilisation Initiative, the official pointed to the West Kowloon Cultural District's two museums as examples of cultural exchange. The Hong Kong Palace Museum collaborated with the Museum of Islamic Art in Doha last year and will partner with the Guimet National Museum of Asian Arts in Paris next month. M+ recently formed a cultural alliance with the Centre Pompidou in Paris and the Museum of Modern Art in New York.
For the Global Governance Initiative, the official highlighted the International Dispute Resolution Organisation (IDRO), which opened its headquarters in Hong Kong with central government support. The IDRO recorded its first successful case in May, a cross-border maritime dispute resolved through mediation. The headquarters, renovated from the old Wan Chai Police Station, symbolises how parties with differences can find diverse solutions through mediation.
The official said these examples demonstrate how Hong Kong can leverage its strengths to contribute to international cooperation. The official also noted that the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences' Hong Kong and Macao Research Centre, established in July with support from the central government's Hong Kong and Macao Affairs Office, is working to build a theoretical framework and academic discourse for 'one country, two systems'. Looking ahead to the 30th anniversary of Hong Kong's return to the motherland next year, the official said Hong Kong must adhere to the 'one country' foundation while leveraging 'two systems' advantages.

summary: 中国、美国和俄罗斯总统周四在中国举行了前所未有的峰会，唐纳德·特朗普称这三人正在“创造历史”。 2026 年 11 月 19 日，在中国南部广东省深圳举行的亚太经合组织 (APEC) 峰会期间，中国国家主席习近平、美国总统唐纳德·特朗普和俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京抵达麒麟山庄举行三边会议。照片：Win McNamee/法新社。特朗普、习近平和普京在深圳麒麟山庄的闭门会晤结束后
content:
中国、美国和俄罗斯总统周四在中国举行了前所未有的峰会，唐纳德·特朗普称这三人正在“创造历史”。 2026 年 11 月 19 日，在中国南部广东省深圳举行的亚太经合组织 (APEC) 峰会期间，中国国家主席习近平、美国总统唐纳德·特朗普和俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京抵达麒麟山庄举行三边会议。照片：Win McNamee/法新社。特朗普、习近平和普京在深圳麒麟山庄的闭门会晤在1小时20分钟后结束。会议一开始，三人围坐在一张深色的大圆桌旁，围绕从核武器到乌克兰战争等重大话题发表了开场白，圆桌中央摆放着粉红色的插花。特朗普表示：“我很高兴这次访问也为我们提供了举行美国、俄罗斯和中国领导人首次三边会晤的机会。” “所以从这个意义上说，我认为在很多其他方面，我们确实在创造历史，”他补充道。分析人士预计，此次峰会的象征意义大于突破性进展，恰逢俄罗斯对乌克兰的攻势已接近五年大关，并引发了世界各地的恐慌和嘲笑。香港深水埗的一个摊位上展示着美国总统唐纳德·特朗普、中国国家主席习近平和俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京等人的面孔的磁铁。
照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP.Xi 告诉他的外长，这三个国家应该“共同维护世界和平与稳定”，而普京则表示，解决乌克兰战争具有共同利益。普京表示：“在解决地区冲突方面，我们两国有许多共同利益，当然也包括乌克兰冲突。”他补充说，他们“对维护国际和平与安全负有共同责任”。他表示，闭门讨论还将涉及粮食和能源安全——这两个领域都因伊朗和乌克兰的冲突而被颠覆。特朗普因与伊朗的战争而陷入困境，这场战争导致石油供应中断并推高了全球消费者价格，而崛起的中国正在寻求加强其在东亚的影响力。 “很高兴见到你” 麒麟山庄峰会引发了人们的担忧，担心这三位有权势的人想要将全球划分为势力范围，例如通过做出影响乌克兰而不是基辅或欧洲的决定。周四早些时候，特朗普和普京举行了自 2025 年 8 月以来的首次会面，这位 80 岁的美国总统称俄罗斯人为他的“朋友”，普京用英语回应：“很高兴见到你。”随后，特朗普和习近平今年第三次聚在一起进行一对一的讨论，美国领导人强调了他们“非常特殊的关系”。 2026 年 5 月 15 日，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普和中国国家主席习近平在北京中南海合影留念。

【原文 English Original】
The presidents of China, the United States and Russia held an unprecedented summit in China on Thursday, with Donald Trump saying the three men were “making history”. China’s President Xi Jinping, US President Donald Trump and Russia’s President Vladimir Putin arrive for a trilateral meeting at Kylin Villa on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Summit in Shenzhen, in China’s southern Guangdong province, on November 19, 2026. Photo: Win McNamee/AFP. The meeting behind closed doors between Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin in Kylin Villa in Shenzhen ended after an hour and 20 minutes. At the start the three men made opening remarks touching on weighty topics from nuclear weapons to the war in Ukraine as they met around a large, dark round table with a pink flower arrangement at its centre. “I’m delighted that this trip has also given us the opportunity for this first ever trilateral meeting between the leaders of the United States, Russia and China,” Trump said. “So in that sense, and I think in lots of other ways, we are really making history,” he added. The summit, which analysts expect to be heavier in symbolism than breakthroughs, comes with Russia’s Ukraine offensive approaching the five-year mark, and has sparked both alarm and derision around the world. Magnets showing faces of US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin, alongside others, are displayed at a stall in Sham Shui Po, Hong Kong. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Xi told his counterparts that the three countries should “jointly safeguard world peace and stability”, while Putin said they had a shared interest to resolve the Ukraine war. “Our countries have many converging interests when it comes to resolving regional conflicts, including, of course, the conflict in Ukraine,” Putin said, adding they had a “shared responsibility for maintaining international peace and security”. He said the closed-door discussions would also touch on food and energy security — both of which have been upended by conflicts in Iran and Ukraine. Trump is bogged down by his war with Iran that has choked oil supplies and pushed up consumer prices worldwide, while an ascendant China is looking to strengthen its hand in East Asia. ‘Nice to meet you’ The Kylin Villa summit has stoked fears that the three powerful men want to divide the globe into spheres of influence, for example by making decisions impacting Ukraine over the heads of Kyiv or Europe. Earlier Thursday, Trump and Putin held a meeting — their first since August 2025 — with the 80-year-old US president calling the Russian his “friend”, who responded in English: “Nice to meet you.” Trump and Xi then came together — for the third time this year — for one-on-one discussions, with the US leader highlighting their “very special relationship”. US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping pose for a photo at Zhongnanhai in Beijing on May 15, 2026. Photo: The White House, via Flickr. Putin, 74, and Xi, 73, held talks on Wednesday — their 50th meeting, the Chinese president said. Beijing, Washington and Moscow have given different accounts of the agenda for the three-way meeting on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum. Washington initially signalled that Ukraine was off the table, before Trump said the war would feature. Xi does not view the conflict as China’s problem to solve. Trump said in his meeting with Xi however that both China and the United States were “looking to both help with respect to the war with Russia and Ukraine”. China said before that the trio will hold “in-depth exchanges on safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability in major-power relations”. Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelensky (right) visits Bucha in April 2022, after the Russian invasion. Photo: Oleksandr Ratushniak. Critics warned that the optics from the meeting will be damaging for the US president — but a fillip to Xi and Putin. The meeting “gives Putin a platform to legitimise his war of aggression over Ukraine with seemingly little repercussions,” said Lyle Morris at the Asia Society Policy Institute. “Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin are playing Donald Trump like a cheap violin,” Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer said. Nuclear disarmament Washington had also flagged up the Iran war and nuclear disarmament as topics of discussion, after a US-Russia bilateral treaty on atomic weapons expired in February. Beijing has long maintained that the United States and Russia must reduce their giant nuclear arsenals before it agrees to talks on its smaller stockpile. China’s nuclear arsenal. Photo: CCTV screenshot. “As the world’s three largest nuclear powers by far, the United States, Russia and China are uniquely positioned to discuss how to reduce the number of nuclear weapons on Earth and also to lessen the risk that those weapons will ever be used,” Trump said. Airport welcome Thursday’s extraordinary meeting preceded equally unusual scenes as the leaders arrived in the southern Chinese city for the talks. Breaking with decades of diplomatic protocol, Xi received Trump at the airport, with the men briefly hugging before a red-carpet greeting complete with cheering children and an air force flyover. This reciprocated the airport greeting Trump gave Xi at Joint Base Andrews in September. “It’s a friendship relationship. It’s a respect relationship,” Trump told Fox News. Takaichi, on her first visit since angering Beijing a year ago with comments about Taiwan, met Putin — relations are also tense — on Wednesday, Tokyo said. Takaichi said Thursday she wanted a “constructive and stable relationship” with China, but Japanese media said she did not manage to get a one-to-one meeting with Xi in Shenzhen. Despite their differences, all the leaders — including Putin — posed for the APEC “family photo” on Thursday in special scarves.

title: China’s Xi to host historic summit with Trump, Putin

summary: 周四，中国、美国和俄罗斯总统在首次三边峰会前与其他亚太领导人合影留念，北京称这次峰会是关于“世界和平”的会谈。 2026 年 11 月 19 日，在中国南部广东省深圳举行的亚太经合组织 (APEC) 峰会上，中国国家主席习近平（右）和美国总统唐纳德·特朗普（左）在领导人合影前合影。照片：Greg Baker/法新社。习近平、特朗普和普京在深圳麒麟山庄举行三方会晤
content:
周四，中国、美国和俄罗斯总统在首次三边峰会前与其他亚太领导人合影留念，北京称这次峰会是关于“世界和平”的会谈。 2026 年 11 月 19 日，在中国南部广东省深圳举行的亚太经合组织 (APEC) 峰会上，中国国家主席习近平（右）和美国总统唐纳德·特朗普（左）在领导人合影前合影。照片：Greg Baker/法新社。习近平、特朗普和普京在深圳麒麟山庄举行三方会晤之际，俄罗斯对乌克兰的血腥攻势已接近五年。因中期选举失败而受伤的特朗普又因与伊朗的战争而陷入困境，而崛起的中国正在寻求加强其在东亚的影响力。这次秘密会议引发了人们的担忧，担心这三位有权势的人可能会寻求将全球划分为势力范围，例如将乌克兰的命运凌驾于基辅或欧洲之上。此前，特朗普和习近平将举行双边讨论，预计将讨论贸易关系以及英伟达间谍丑闻笼罩下的人工智能潜在共同规则。北京、华盛顿和莫斯科对亚太经济合作组织（APEC）论坛期间的会议内容给出了不同的描述。在特朗普表示战争将成为焦点之前，华盛顿最初表示不考虑乌克兰问题。
习近平并不认为这场冲突是中国需要解决的问题。克里姆林宫表示，议程尚未最终确定，但在会议上很难避免讨论乌克兰问题，会议预计将持续“不超过一个小时”。 2026 年 5 月 20 日，孩子们在北京人民大会堂举行的欢迎仪式上向中国国家主席习近平（左）和俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京致意。照片：克里姆林宫。自 2022 年发动全面进攻以来，普京在很大程度上受到西方大国的回避，他在周三的亚太经合组织会议上表示，西方对其国家的制裁“失败了”。 “在军事政治风险上升之际，迫切需要的是……对话而不是最后通牒，”他说。中国仅表示，三方将“就维护世界和平、促进大国关系战略稳定进行深入交流”。批评者警告说，这次会议的景象将对美国总统造成损害。参议院民主党领袖查克·舒默表示：“习近平和弗拉基米尔·普京正在像演奏廉价小提琴一样演奏唐纳德·特朗普。”盛大的欢迎 根据华盛顿的说法，在美俄双边原子武器条约二月份到期后，伊朗战争和核裁军问题也将成为讨论的焦点。然而，北京长期以来一直坚持认为，美国和俄罗斯应该先削减其庞大的核武库，然后才同意就其较小的核武库进行谈判。 “看，我们有 4000 件核武器。
俄罗斯拥有 3,800 枚核武器。中国现在拥有四五百枚，但他们将会赶上。你知道，在 10 年的时间里，他们正在行动。”特朗普告诉福克斯新闻。特朗普表示，他还考虑与普京以及朝鲜领导人金正恩进行一对一会谈，尽管后者没有出席会议。朝鲜领导人金正恩（左）和美国总统唐纳德·特朗普（右）。照片：白宫/Flickr。习近平在

【原文 English Original】
The presidents of China, the United States and Russia posed for a photo with other Asia-Pacific leaders on Thursday ahead of their first ever trilateral summit, billed by Beijing as talks about “world peace”. China’s President Xi Jinping (R) and US President Donald Trump (L) pose for a photo before leaders take a group photo during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Summit in Shenzhen, in China’s southern Guangdong Province, on November 19, 2026. Photo: Greg Baker/AFP. The three-way meeting between Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin at the Kylin Villa in Shenzhen comes with Russia’s bloody offensive in Ukraine approaching the five-year mark. Trump, wounded by the midterm election debacle, is bogged down by his war with Iran, and an ascendant China is looking to strengthen its hand in East Asia. The conclave has stoked fears that the three powerful men may seek to divide the globe into spheres of influence, for example deciding the fate of Ukraine over the heads of Kyiv or Europe. Beforehand Trump and Xi were due to hold bilateral discussions expected to touch on trade ties and potentially common rules for AI under the cloud of the Nvidia spy scandal . Beijing, Washington and Moscow have given different accounts of what they expect to discuss from the powwow on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum. Washington initially signalled that Ukraine was off the table, before Trump said the war would feature. Xi does not view the conflict as China’s problem to solve. The Kremlin has said that the agenda had not been finalised, but it would be hard to avoid discussing Ukraine at the meeting, which is set to last “no more than an hour”. Children greet Chinese President Xi Jinping (left) and Russian President Vladimir Putin during the welcome ceremony at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing on May 20, 2026. Photo: The Kremlin. Putin, largely shunned by Western powers since his 2022 full-scale offensive, told the APEC gathering on Wednesday that Western sanctions on his country had “failed”. “At a time when military-political risks are on the rise, what is desperately needed is… dialogue rather than ultimatums,” he said. China has said only that the trio will hold “in-depth exchanges on safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability in major-power relations”. Critics warned that the optics from the meeting will be damaging for the US president. “Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin are playing Donald Trump like a cheap violin,” Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer said. Lavish welcome Also up for discussion are the Iran war and nuclear disarmament, according to Washington, after a US-Russia bilateral treaty on atomic weapons expired in February. However, Beijing has long maintained that the United States and Russia should reduce their giant nuclear arsenals before it agrees to talks on its smaller stockpile. “Look, we have 4,000 nuclear weapons. Russia has 3,800 nuclear weapons. China now has four or five hundred, but they’re going to catch (up). You know, over a 10-year period, they’re moving,” Trump told Fox News. Trump has said he is also eyeing one-on-one talks with Putin as well as North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, though the latter is not present at the conference. North Korean Leader Kim Jong-un (left) and US President Donald Trump (right). Photo: The White House/Flickr. In a sign of the importance that China is placing on the trilateral summit, Xi gave Trump an extravagant welcome on Wednesday. Breaking with decades of diplomatic protocol, the Chinese leader personally received Trump at the airport, with the men briefly hugging before a red-carpet greeting complete with cheering children and an air-force flyover. It was the first time that China’s paramount leader had welcomed a foreign dignitary in person for decades, and reciprocated the airport greeting Trump gave Xi at Joint Base Andrews in September. “It’s a friendship relationship. It’s a respect relationship,” Trump told Fox News from Shenzhen. Xi “has never gone to the airport to meet somebody… It was a great respect, and I appreciate that. That’s a big win for us. It’s a big win for China too,” Trump said. ‘Serene authority’ “I look forward to an in-depth exchange of views with you on major issues concerning China-US relations, Asia-Pacific cooperation, and the global landscape, with the aim of advancing a constructive, strategically stable relationship between our two nations,” Xi told Trump, according to Chinese state news agency Xinhua. In contrast, Putin was welcomed at the airport by Cai Qi, China’s fifth-ranked leader, in accordance with regular protocol. Other world leaders at the APEC meeting include Japan’s Sanae Takaichi, South Korea’s Lee Jae Myung, Canada’s Mark Carney and Australia’s Anthony Albanese. Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi (left) and Chinese President Xi Jinping at the APEC summit in Gyeongju, South Korea, on October 31, 2025. Photo: Sanae Takaichi, via X. Takaichi, on her first visit to China since angering Beijing a year ago with comments about Taiwan, met Putin — with whom relations are also tense — on Wednesday, Tokyo said. Despite their differences, all the leaders — including Putin — posed for the APEC “family photo” on Thursday in matching scarves. Apart from the centrepiece trilateral, the group was also expected to discuss a range of other topics, including trade policy and artificial intelligence. Xi opened the APEC leaders’ meeting on Thursday with a call to “reduce barriers to trade and investment”. Analysts believe the day’s events will be heavily scripted, but underline that the personalities may yet spring surprises. “Typically, when Chinese leaders host meetings, every detail is nailed down and China’s leader is positioned to project an air of serene authority and control,” said Ryan Hass at the Brookings Institution. “Given the other leaders involved though — Trump and Putin — there is only so much choreography that can be done to eliminate unexpected moments,” Hass told AFP.

content:
ICIJ 的中国资本调查揭露了全球最大银行中国工商银行 (ICBC) 的伦敦分行如何例行公事地为企业提供资金以推动北京的地缘政治议程，有时甚至在此过程中藐视自己的合规规则。 ICIJ 与 23 家媒体合作伙伴合作，获得了工银伦敦泄露的 480 万份内部文件，包括贷款申请表、尽职调查报告、了解你的客户文件和内部电子邮件往来。为了更好地了解工行伦敦业务，ICIJ数据团队剖析了2010年至2024年期间的200多份贷款协议和修正案。ICIJ发现，在审查的协议和修正案中，工银伦敦至少与另一家中国国有商业银行合作。在中国的银行中，中国银行脱颖而出，成为工银伦敦分行的主要中方合作伙伴：双方签署了 102 项协议。 ICIJ 的分析显示，这家中国银行业巨头的伦敦分行通常与其他中国和国际银行合作，达成价值数亿美元甚至更多的贷款协议。 ICIJ 发现了 36 项贷款协议和修正案，其中一半或以上的资金是由中国贷方提供的。其中 16 个案例的财务承诺完全来自中资银行。
ICIJ 的一项审查发现，作为对该行客户尽职调查过程一部分的工行文件显示，该行有时会淡化合规问题，或以其他方式证明继续与其被归类为高风险的客户开展业务是合理的。 在赞比亚，工行在加剧该国债务负担、造成对中国贷款的依赖以及给赞比亚人造成多年困难方面发挥了作用。在英国，中国工商银行的银行管理人员无视其一位中国客户在美国法院面临的法律风险，以便该银行能够为该公司收购英国竞争对手并巩固其市场份额提供资金。下面的案例研究揭示了一家银行在中国党国议程的推进与其自身的全球商业野心之间取得平衡的内部运作方式。无视红灯 01 2024年5月，工商银行的高风险客户名单包括全球燃料贸易商和分销商Puma Energy的融资部门以及大股东Trafigura Pte.有限公司是一家注册并总部位于新加坡的贸易巨头，主要贸易业务位于瑞士，以及另外两家托克实体。尽管中国工商银行对 Puma 和 Trafigura 的担忧至少可以追溯到 2015 年，但 ICIJ 发现 2015 年至 2024 年间涉及 Puma 和 Trafigura 的 19 项银团信贷安排协议，总价值达 387 亿美元。 ICBC 的伦敦实体在这些贷款中总共承诺提供 14 亿美元。
2015年，工商银行加大了对Puma旗下融资工具Puma International Financing的尽职调查力度；在其2015年5月的强化尽职调查（EDD）报告中，将该公司的贿赂风险评为“高”。 当时，Puma的股东包括安哥拉国有石油公司Sonangol和Cochan Holdings LLC（一家由安哥拉总统顾问Leopoldino Fragoso do Nascimento创立并担任主席的投资公司）。该报告承认，媒体广泛报道了涉及安哥拉高级官员的贿赂和腐败行为，其中包括当时的总统若泽·爱德华多·多斯桑托斯及其子女，以及Sonangol、Cochan和Nascimento。尽管如此，工行仍对大部分逆回购进行了描述

【原文 English Original】
ICIJ’s China Capital investigation revealed how the London units of the world’s largest bank, the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC), routinely financed companies to push Beijing’s geopolitical agenda, sometimes flouting their own compliance rules in the process. ICIJ, in collaboration with 23 media partners, obtained 4.8 million internal documents leaked from ICBC London, including loan application forms, due diligence reports, know-your-client documents and internal email exchanges. To better understand ICBC’s London operations, the ICIJ data team dissected more than 200 loan agreements and amendments dated from 2010 to 2024. ICIJ found that ICBC London partnered with at least one other Chinese state-owned commercial bank in more than half of the agreements and amendments reviewed. Among the Chinese lenders, Bank of China stands out as the main Chinese partner of ICBC London: They joined forces in 102 agreements. ICIJ’s analysis shows that the London units of the Chinese banking giant usually partnered with other Chinese and international banks on loan agreements often worth hundreds of millions of dollars—or more. ICIJ identified 36 loan agreements and amendments for which half or more of the money was provided by Chinese lenders. In 16 of those cases, the financial commitments were entirely from Chinese banks. ICBC documents prepared as part of the due diligence process on the bank’s clients show how the bank at times downplayed compliance problems or otherwise justified continued business with clients it had classified as high risk, an ICIJ review found. In Zambia, ICBC played a role in exacerbating the country’s debt burden, creating dependency on Chinese loans and contributing to years-long difficulties for Zambians. In the U.K., ICBC bank officers disregarded legal risks faced in a U.S. court by one of their Chinese clients so the bank could finance the company’s acquisition of a British competitor and consolidate its market share. The case studies below reveal the inner workings of a bank balancing the advancement of the agenda of the Chinese party-state with its own global commercial ambitions. Ignoring Red Lights 01 In May 2024, ICBC’s high-risk client list included the financing arm of global fuel trader and distributor Puma Energy, along with a major shareholder Trafigura Pte. Ltd., a trading giant registered and headquartered in Singapore with major trading operations in Switzerland, and two other Trafigura entities. Despite ICBC's concerns about Puma and Trafigura dating back to at least 2015, ICIJ identified 19 syndicated credit facility agreements involving Puma and Trafigura, between 2015 and 2024, with a combined value of $38.7 billion. ICBC's London entities committed a total of $1.4 billion across those facilities. In 2015, ICBC escalated its due diligence of Puma’s financing vehicle, Puma International Financing; in its May 2015 Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) report, it rated the company’s bribery risk as high. At the time, Puma's shareholders included Angola's state-owned oil company Sonangol and Cochan Holdings LLC, an investment company founded and chaired by Angolan presidential adviser Leopoldino Fragoso do Nascimento. The report acknowledged extensive adverse media coverage alleging bribery and corruption involving senior Angolan officials, including then-President José Eduardo dos Santos and his children, as well as Sonangol, Cochan and Nascimento. Still, ICBC characterized much of the adverse reporting as “rumour based and unfounded” and continued the relationship, subject to enhanced monitoring. In February 2020, ICBC’s EDD report again identified allegations centered on Nascimento’s close ties to former President dos Santos and speculation in media reports and elsewhere that he had used political connections to acquire a stake in Puma Energy while serving as a public official. The report also noted that Nascimento had faced investigations into alleged corruption, conflicts of interest and money laundering in several countries. Yet ICBC cited reasons for discounting the risks, noting that Nascimento did “not appear to have been convicted” of wrongdoing. In December 2021, the U.S. Treasury sanctioned Nascimento and Cochan, saying Nascimento and another Angolan official had embezzled billions from the Angolan government. In 2025, an Angolan court convicted Nascimento of fraud, document forgery, money laundering and influence peddling. Likewise, ICBC's October 2019 Enhanced Due Diligence report came after a highly public Brazilian corruption investigation into allegations that commodity traders, including Trafigura, had bribed employees of Petrobras, Brazil’s state-owned and state-controlled oil company. A month earlier, Reuters reported allegations that senior Trafigura executives Mike Wainwright and José Larocca knew about the bribes. But ICBC's EDD report referred only to "two high-ranking executives” at Trafigura, without identifying them, despite separately listing both men as key controllers of Trafigura. Wainwright's adverse-media assessment was marked "No." ICBC continued the relationship, citing Trafigura's status as a longstanding "strategic client," the participation of major international banks in syndicated loans, its compliance controls and the absence of suspicious activity detected by ICBC. In 2024, Trafigura Beheer B.V., the Dutch-registered former parent company of the Trafigura Group, pleaded guilty in the U.S. to conspiring to violate U.S. anti-bribery laws in a scheme that ran from approximately 2003 to 2014. The companies also reached a settlement agreement with Brazilian authorities. Read responses Responses Trafigura: In response to ICIJ's questions, a Trafigura spokesperson said lender due diligence was a normal part of doing business and that the company cooperated with lenders' reviews, supported by its public financial and sustainability disclosures. Regarding the Petrobras bribery case, the spokesperson referred to Trafigura's 2024 statement announcing the resolution of the U.S. investigation, in which the company said the misconduct involved former employees or agents and was inconsistent with its principles and code of conduct. The statement said U.S. authorities had recognized improvements to Trafigura's anti-corruption compliance procedures. Puma: didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. Nascimento: didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. Angolan government: didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. Cochan: ICIJ could not successfully contact Cochan for comment. Sonangol: didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. A legal representative for Mike Wainwright didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. José Larocca: didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. ICBC: didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. Main borrowers Puma International Financing S.A., Trafigura Group Pte. Ltd., Trafigura Pte. Ltd., Trafigura Trading LLC Amount $1.4 billionTotal loan commitments Start dates of loans 2015-2024 From the China Capital files PUMA In their own words: There is a wealth of adverse news in the public domain citing the Angolan Government's bribery and corruption and monopolisation of various industries in Angola.Risk From the China Capital files TRAFIGURA In their own words: The risks of money laundering, sanctions and bribery and corruption are heightened [...] and thus this poses an increased reputational risk to the Bank.Risk Trafigura is an existing and strategic client of the Bank.Mitigating factors Financing Kleptocrats 02 ICBC started lending to Socar, Azerbaijan’s state oil and gas concern, in 2015 when ICBC London took part in a revolving credit facility to one of the company’s subsidiaries, Socar Trading SA. Even though the bank decided to exit this facility in 2019 because of the company's “underperformance and ongoing restructuring," a review of ICBC documents shows that under the head office’s encouragement, ICBC’s London and Turkey offices maintained close connection with Socar. Bank officers in an internal memo noted “Azerbaijan's geopolitical importance in the area's political and economic landscape, and its longstanding partnership with super oil majors,” adding “SOCAR is a strategically important client for ICBC in view of supporting China's 2013 One-Belt One-Road policy." ICBC London committed to at least three additional loans, each between $25 million and $89 million, even as the bank continued to list Socar among high-risk clients, with one document stating: “the risks of money laundering, sanctions and bribery and corruption are heightened." Corporate bank officers underlined the risks presented by the nature of Socar’s business and its jurisdiction, Azerbaijan; the fact that all the members of its board of directors were, at the time, identified as politically exposed persons, including the president and 12 vice presidents; Socar’s lack of transparency and accountability; and that the company had recently featured in major international corruption scandals. Yet the same year that ICBC listed these risks, 2021, the bank agreed to lend Socar $89 million. ICBC and Socar had deepened their ties in 2018, when the bank’s London branch listed $1.58 billion worth of green bonds on the London Stock Exchange, and Azerbaijan's State Oil Fund, SOFAZ, decided to invest $150 million. Socar, which sells oil and gas on the state’s behalf, contributed about 90% of SOFAZ’s 2017 revenue. The Organized Crime and Corruption Reporting Project later reported that leaked documents from inside British Petroleum exposed that two Socar subsidiaries were set to siphon off more than $1.7 billion from the Shah Deniz 2 gas project through padded contracts and fake charges. Socar denied the allegations. Read response Response Socar: didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. SOFAZ: didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. ICBC: didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. Main borrower Socar and its subsidiaries Amount $217 million (4 loans)Total loan commitments Start dates of loans 2015-2021 From the China Capital files In their own words: Given Azerbaijan’s geopolitical importance in the area’s political and economic landscape, and its longstanding partnership with super oil majors, SOCAR is a strategically important client for ICBC in view of supporting China’s 2013 One-Belt One-Road policy aimed at creating infrastructure and establishing links among the Eurasian countries.Risk Consolidating Market Share 03 ICBC records show bank risk management officials looking past the potentially illegal actions of a Chinese customer seeking a loan to buy out one of its competitors. In 2017 ICBC London Branch agreed to back China’s Hytera Communications Corp. Ltd.’s acquisition of Sepura PLC, a British telecommunications competitor in the mobile radio communications sector. Hytera designs and manufactures professional mobile communications devices commonly used by law enforcement agencies worldwide — including two-way radios, a market that at the time was expected to be worth $7.3 billion by 2025. The agreement with ICBC London, which was the only lender involved, allowed Hytera to borrow up to $57.1 million over three years. Sepura shareholders had approved the $92.7 million acquisition in January 2017 but antitrust authorities in the UK and Germany, where governments relied on Sepura’s technology, stalled the acquisition. Spanish antitrust authorities also assessed the transaction, which was eventually approved in May of that year. While conducting their due diligence work to approve the loan in early 2017, ICBC London employees discovered that Motorola Solutions Inc., another competitor in the mobile telecommunications market, had filed a lawsuit pending against Hytera in a U.S. federal court for alleged patent infringement and industrial espionage. The bank’s compliance officers allowed the loan to go forward anyway, adding a handwritten note on a printout of an article about the suit that the case wasn’t related to any major financial crime. The article mentioned, however, that Motorola accused Hytera of hiring ex-Motorola employees after they had allegedly stolen thousands of pages of confidential documents. By early 2020, while Hytera was repaying the loan ICBC employees flagged a problem — Hytera had lost its U.S. case. In a briefing note to the bank’s credit committee at the end of April, they wrote that the verdict “confirms that Hytera engaged in illegal trade secret theft and copyright infringement, validating Motorola's global litigation against Hytera.” Following the U.S. court verdict ICBC London received an injunction from a British court ordering the bank to freeze Hytera assets, potentially stopping the repayment of the loan. Seven Hytera employees were later indicted for their alleged roles in the thefts from Motorola; one pleaded guilty in 2022 to charges of conspiracy to steal trade secrets and is awaiting sentencing. Hytera pleaded guilty in 2025 to “conspiracy to steal trade secrets” and was fined $50 million. Hytera was also ordered to pay Motorola more than $400 million in a separate lawsuit. In 2021, the U.S. Federal Communications Commission published a list of Chinese manufacturers, including Hytera, which “pose an unacceptable risk to the national security of the United States.” The same year, the British government passed the National Security and Investment Act which gave heightened power to the government to proactively review acquisitions in 17 sensitive sectors, including communications. Hytera sold its entire shareholding in Sepura in July 2022. Read responses Responses Hytera: didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. In an email to ICIJ, Sepura said that "neither Sepura PLC nor its shareholders or management at the time were involved in Hytera’s choice of funding for its acquisition of Sepura” and that the company “had no customer relationship with ICBC and held no accounts with the bank” following the acquisition. It also said that it was not “a party to the litigation brought by Motorola against Hytera concerning Motorola’s intellectual property” and that “the technology at issue was distinct from that developed and used by Sepura in its own products”. “Sepura's proprietary technology and IPR were ring-fenced by statutory undertakings, as mandated and defined by the UK government and accepted by Hytera.” Sepura said it “has had no further interaction with Hytera since the sale” in 2022. ICBC: didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. Borrower Project Shortway Ltd. (ultimately owned by Hytera Communications Corp. Ltd.) Amount up to $57.1 millionTotal loan commitments Start date of loans May 2017 From the China Capital files In their own words Handwritten note on an article: Not major financial crime issues relatedRisk Buying your backyard 04 ICBC participated in syndicated loans — financing provided by a group of lenders who share the risk — for a Chinese commercial real estate venture that went bust and defaulted on its loans, according to internal loan agreements and property assessments reviewed by ICIJ. In 2017, Chinese real estate tycoon Chen Hongtian and his wife bought two office towers in London’s trendy Canary Wharf commercial district, hoping to convert their $900 million investment into a profitable venture. ICBC London described the area as “one of the world’s premier commercial districts,” with “24 office buildings with around 200 shops, bars, and restaurants” according to a 2022 assessment of 5 Churchill Place’s value by the real estate company managing the asset. The real estate firm’s assessment came as the bank and other creditors looked to liquidate the assets of the embattled tycoon who had found himself short on cash and unable to make payments. By then, ICBC London Branch had committed $205 million out of roughly half a billion in loans made with other banks to Chen’s companies in the British Virgin Islands, through which he and his family owned the London properties. One of those properties, at 20 Canada Square, was mainly occupied by two Western firms, according to a 2022 ICBC internal credit report. But the properties couldn’t compete with more modern and energy-efficient real estate, and their value plummeted. By April 2023 ICBC London had reclassified the loan to Cheung Pang Holdings Ltd., a BVI company through which Chen owned some units of the Canada Square property, as “non performing” and added the borrower to its watchlist. Around the same time that ICBC was reviewing the properties, the UK government passed the Economic Crime (Transparency and Enforcement) Act which required overseas entities that hold property in England and Wales to file beneficial ownership information with the company registry. A report published in 2017 by the U.S. Government Accountability Office warned that leasing space in foreign-owned buildings "could present security risks such as espionage and unauthorized cyber and physical access.” The UK’s National Security and Investment Act took effect in January 2022, but real estate was not among the sensitive sectors subject to its mandatory screening requirements for acquisitions. Read responses Responses Chen Hongtian/Cheung Kei group: The Cheung Kei group didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. In statement posted on its website in 2023 the group said that “like all heavy asset holders”, it was “experiencing a phase of cash problems” and that its “overall asset scale and asset quality” were “very high, with a low debt ratio among peers.” At the time the group was “selling some equity in some assets and actively negotiating repayment arrangements with relevant financial institutions” and said it “believed that subsequent financial institution issues will be properly resolved.” ICBC London: didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. Main borrowers Jovial Link Holdings Ltd. for 5 Churchill Place; Cheung Pang Holdings Ltd., Cheung Kwan Holdings Ltd. for 20 Canada Square (London properties) Start dates of loans 2022 Amount $61.7M / $143.5MTotal loan commitments From the China Capital files In their own words: About 5 Churchill Place, from a credit loan application: The deal as outlined herein offers ICBC London an ideal opportunity to assist an incoming Chinese client in the purchase of a major “trophy” asset that is both well let to tenants of significant covenant strengths and well located within the popular Canary Wharf developmentRisk Trapping In Debt 05 ICBC records on Zambia show a lender watching a borrower facing growing financial risks, while quietly putting protections in place for its own loans. ICBC financed a range of major projects in the country, providing loans for government-owned housing, a hospital, an airport and power projects running to hundreds of millions of dollars. Among them was a $285 million loan approved in 2010 to ZESCO, Zambia's state-owned power company, for two power transmission projects. Between 2015 and 2018, ICBC provided or participated in at least six more loans to ZESCO, totaling $1.2 billion according to AidData estimates, even as the bank was aware of mounting financial pressures on both Zambia and ZESCO. By 2017, a sovereign risk assessment in the bank's files described Zambia as facing limited financing options, rising interest costs, and substantial debt—and specifically pointed to financial pressures on ZESCO. Government net debt had climbed from 23% of GDP in 2013 to an estimated 57% in 2017, while debt costs consumed nearly a quarter of government revenue. ICBC had classified ZESCO as a high-risk client since 2018, citing Zambia's country risk, politically exposed persons and historical adverse media coverage including bribery and corruption allegations, according to a 2023 internal report. Despite these concerns, the bank continued its lending relationship with ZESCO, requiring annual reviews. ICBC built protections into its lending. ZESCO maintained a debt-service reserve account at ICBC London for repayments on the $285 million loan. Money deposited into the account could only be withdrawn by ICBC's head office, which was also the lender, agent and security trustee. ZESCO’s financial precarity triggered a cascade of credit problems. By March 2020, its failure to pay Maamba Collieries Ltd., a Zambian power supplier, had left Maamba unable to meet its own loan obligations to ICBC and other lenders. ICBC records show that lenders sent letters to Zambia's Ministry of Finance seeking government support, contacted Chinese state-owned insurer Sinosure and discussed restructuring the loan. ICBC officials warned that Maamba's loan would be classified as non-performing if payments remained overdue for more than 90 days. The documents offer a window into how the bank continued banking a financially strained borrower while using safeguards to limit its own losses. title: Europe and China 1 – The Arrival of the People’s Republic
zh_title: 欧洲与中国 1 – 中华人民共和国的到来
summary: 这是有关中国与欧洲关系的三部分系列文章的第一部分。 20世纪90年代，天安门广场的阴影笼罩了欧洲与中国的贸易关系。 1989年对抗议者的屠杀标志着独裁统治的回归，政治改革的希望破灭了。欧洲公司撤退，实施武器禁运，孤立“北京屠夫”的政治压力也越来越大。然而，到了这个十年末，中国胜利地加入了世界贸易组织（WTO），其经济快速增长，随着“全球化”这个新词的出现，世界已经站在了门口。
content:
这是有关中国与欧洲关系的三部分系列文章的第一部分。 20世纪90年代，天安门广场的阴影笼罩了欧洲与中国的贸易关系。 1989年对抗议者的屠杀标志着独裁统治的回归，政治改革的希望破灭了。欧洲公司撤退，实施武器禁运，孤立“北京屠夫”的政治压力也越来越大。然而，到了这个十年末，中国胜利地加入了世界贸易组织（WTO），其经济正在快速增长，随着“全球化”这个新词成为每次企业峰会的议程，世界已经来到了门口。为了重现这一转变，历史学家必须首先确定其背后的政治人物。即使天安门上的鲜血被冲洗干净——当未来的国家主席习近平的妻子、歌手彭丽媛为戒严部队唱小夜曲时——许多中国领导人知道他们犯了一个可怕的错误。其中包括习近平的父亲、两次被清洗的退伍军人习仲勋，他公开赞扬镇压“反革命暴乱”的“明智”和“坚决”决定，但私下里对经济改革的挫折表示哀悼。习仲勋亲自执掌南方经济强国广东，在20世纪80年代把它变成了吸引外资的世界工厂。他是影响 1989 年后中国下一届领导人选择的造王者之一。
这两名新面孔是从沿海贸易大都市上海走上来的。江泽民是上海共产党的领导人，也是一名受过苏联训练的工程师，后来成为国家主席和党的领导人。然而，关键人物却是一位名叫朱镕基的市长，他是一位出生于1928年、头脑敏锐的技术官僚。他先后担任央行行长和总理。天安门事件发生时，两人曾监督和平结束中国商业首都的大规模抗议活动。上海没有发生大屠杀。相反，朱在电视上发出严厉警告，当局则部署警察和民兵慢慢平息示威活动。上海很快就恢复了商业秩序。欧洲公司是浦东新金融区的第一批投资者。两位领导人都决心让中国向世界经济开放，不顾党内左派的强烈反对。他们的活动可以通过日内瓦世贸组织的档案来追踪，这是谈判的宝贵指南。获取最新注册以接收定期电子邮件并随时了解 CEPA 的工作。

This is the first of a three-part series on China’s relationship with Europe. In the 1990s, the shadow of Tiananmen Square fell across Europe’s trade relations with China. The massacre of protesters in 1989 marked a return to dictatorship and wiped out hopes of political reform. European firms drew back, an arms embargo was imposed, and political pressure grew to isolate “the butchers of Beijing.” Yet by the end of the decade China had swept triumphantly into the World Trade Organisation (WTO), its economy was growing fast, and the world was at its door as a new word, “globalization,” set the agenda at every corporate summit. To reconstruct the turnaround, a historian must first identify the political personalities behind it. Even as the blood was hosed off Tiananmen — and while the future President Xi Jinping’s wife, the singer Peng Liyuan, serenaded the martial law troops — many Chinese leaders knew they had made a terrible blunder. They included Xi Jinping’s father, the twice-purged army veteran Xi Zhongxun, who paid homage in public to the “wise” and “resolute” decision to suppress “a counter-revolutionary riot” but in private mourned the setback to economic reform. Xi Zhongxun himself had taken charge of the southern powerhouse of Guangdong, turning it into a workshop for the world that drew in foreign investment through the 1980s. He was one of the kingmakers who influenced the choice of China’s next leaders after 1989. The new faces were two men who had stepped up from the coastal trading metropolis of Shanghai. Jiang Zemin, the Communist Party boss in Shanghai, a Soviet-trained engineer, became President and leader of the party. Yet the key figure turned out to be a dynamo called Zhu Rongji, the city’s mayor, a sharp-witted technocrat born in 1928. In succession, he became governor of the central bank and prime minister. The duo had overseen a peaceful end to mass protests in China’s commercial capital at the time of Tiananmen. There was no massacre in Shanghai. Instead, Zhu went on television to issue a grim warning, and the authorities deployed police and militia to quieten the demonstrations slowly. Shanghai was soon back in business. European companies were in the first wave of investors in the city’s new financial district of Pudong. Both leaders were determined to open China up to the world economy, defying vocal opposition from leftists in the party. Their campaign can be traced through the archives of the WTO in Geneva, an invaluable guide to the negotiations. Get the Latest Sign up to receive regular emails and stay informed about CEPA's work. As early as 1986, China had applied to join the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT), but the major trading powers had decided to transform the GATT into a new body that would govern services as well as trade from January 1, 1995. It was too soon for China to join the new World Trade Organization at its birth, but negotiations began in earnest. The EU formed a negotiating bloc in rounds of bilateral talks between China and all its partners, which the WTO would then orchestrate into a package. Accession was vital to China, as Zhu Rongji argued in party councils. In 1993, for example, the People’s Republic recorded a trade deficit of more than $12bn, due to the cost of imports for modernization. At the same time, China’s foreign trade had soared to $195bn from $20bn in 1978, the start of the “reform and open up” era. John Bond, the chairman of HSBC Holdings, heard Zhu speak and realized that the Communist cadre had posed a modern version of the famous “Needham Question” raised by the Cambridge polymath, Joseph Needham, of why modern science had enjoyed a meteoric rise in Europe but not in China. “How can 22% of the world’s population account for less than 4% of the world’s GNP?” Bond asked. The WTO documents show the intricacy and the scale of that challenge. The rewards were obvious. In the five years after 1990, Guangdong Province, the former fiefdom of Xi Jinping’s father, saw an expansion across key industries of 40% every 12 months, according to the official Statistical Yearbook for 1996. Formidable obstacles remained. Zhu Rongji fought battles in Beijing to push through a 1994 package of changes to banking, finance, taxation, investment, foreign exchange and foreign trade. The working party in Geneva met behind closed doors 21 times between March 1996 and September 2001. The Europeans pressed hard on intellectual property, copyright protection, patents, trademarks (matters of great concern to Germany), test data, trade secrets, government procurement, minority shareholder rights, and judicial remedies. The WTO working party report alone ran to almost 200 pages. In the end, Europe had a deal. The fate of China was put into American hands. Between September and December 2001, the Clinton administration waged cliff-edge negotiations with the Chinese that remain controversial to this day. A myth has grown that China was ushered into the WTO by vested interests pushing a globalization and free trade agenda. The record shows that China’s road to accession was, in fact, long, painstaking and hard-fought. The final agreement imposed harsher conditions on China than any other nation when its membership became formal on December 11, 2001. It ran to 1,500 pages and weighed 13 kg (29 lbs.). Zhu Rongji saw his country become the world’s second largest economy, the biggest exporter, and the world’s largest holder of foreign currency reserves. He died earlier this year. “It was win-win,’ said the Hong Kong representative in Geneva from 1994 to 2002, Stuart Harbinson. “That was the conventional wisdom.” Michael Sheridan is a veteran British foreign correspondent and is the author of ‘ The Gate to China ’, an acclaimed history of Hong Kong, and ‘ The Red Emperor: Xi Jinping and His New China ’, which is published by Hachette Books and has been translated into a dozen languages, including Ukrainian, Polish, and Japanese. title: Community-Focused Academic Brings AI Tools to Colorado Farmers
zh_title: 以社区为中心的学术界为科罗拉多州农民带来人工智能工具
summary: 科罗拉多州东部的许多农民和牧场主对人工智能感到好奇，但他们没有当地精通技术的人来向他们展示如何使用人工智能。薛“爱丽丝”董已将此作为她的工作。董是 IEEE 高级会员，也是科罗拉多州立大学推广部门（CSU 的外展部门）的推广区域专家。她在洛根县工作，为科罗拉多州东北角的 10 个县农业区提供服务。她的工作是将大学研究转化为对居住在那里的人们的实际帮助。薛“爱丽丝”东 雇主 科罗拉多州立大学洛根县扩建项目 Tit
content:
科罗拉多州东部的许多农民和牧场主对人工智能感到好奇，但他们没有当地精通技术的人来向他们展示如何使用人工智能。薛“爱丽丝”董已将此作为她的工作。董是 IEEE 高级会员，也是科罗拉多州立大学推广部门（CSU 的外展部门）的推广区域专家。她在洛根县工作，为科罗拉多州东北角的 10 个县农业区提供服务。她的工作是将大学研究转化为对居住在那里的人们的实际帮助。薛“爱丽丝”董 雇主 科罗拉多州立大学洛根县推广 职称 推广区域专家 会员等级 高级会员 母校内蒙古师范大学，位于呼和浩特；北京师范大学；纽约州立大学环境科学与林业学院，位于锡拉丘兹；科罗拉多州立大学全球分校 她构建了人工智能驱动的农业旅游聊天机器人 (AgriTourismAI.com)，帮助农民和牧场主启动和经营“农业旅游”业务。农业旅游是指农民向游客开放他们的土地以进行娱乐、教育或购物活动。常见的例子包括采摘自己的果园、如何种植蔬菜的课程以及手工产品的销售。董还举办研讨会，向农民和牧场主展示如何使用人工智能工具来帮助发展和管理他们的业务。她说她将自己视为大学和农村之间的纽带。 “我们（推广专家）充当桥梁，”她说。
“我们将校园与我们服务的农村社区联系起来。”许多农民和牧场主年龄较大，通常没有接受过技术培训。他们的子孙常常离开农场到城市工作，或者无法教他们新工具。如果没有帮助，人工智能的好处可能会与农民失之交臂。 Dong 的研讨会为他们提供了一条出路。Dong 凭借她的 AgriPivot AI Agent 入围 2026 年 GenAI for Good Challenge 决赛。该挑战赛由 IEEE Humanarian Technologies 和联合国国际电信联盟组织，她的项目是从 79 个国家的 318 个团队中选出的。她还获得了国家推广技术社区 (NETC) 颁发的 2026 年创新奖，以及国家社区发展推广专业人员协会 (NACDEP) 颁发的 2025 年国家和西部地区教育技术奖。作为首席研究员或联合首席研究员，她获得了七项竞争性资助，总额超过 25 万美元，其中包括由农业部国家食品和农业研究所支持的资金。董出生于北京，从小就热爱设计和解决问题。她的父母都是医生。小时候，她喜欢画新的、有创意的东西。她说，素描可以让她用图片解决脑海中的问题，并将它们作为实际设计写在纸上。这个习惯逐渐成为她与周围环境相处的一种方式。
她说：“我一直热衷于创造一些有形的东西来解决现实世界中的问题。”她并不将自己的人生方向归功于任何一位导师。相反，她说她所有的老师都帮助她为她的职业生涯奠定了基础。她就读于位于呼和浩特的内蒙古师范大学，这是一所培训教师的机构。 2013 年，她在那里获得了两个学士学位——一个是地理科学学士学位，另一个是教育学士学位。然后，她获得了课程和教学硕士学位

【原文 English Original】
Many farmers and ranchers in eastern Colorado are curious about artificial intelligence, but they don’t have a local tech-savvy person to show them how to use it. Xue “Alice” Dong has made that her job. Dong, an IEEE senior member, is an extension regional specialist with the Colorado State University Extension , CSU’s outreach arm. She works in Logan County and serves a 10-county farming area in Colorado’s northeast corner. Her job is to turn university research into practical help for the people who live there. Xue “Alice” Dong Employer Colorado State University Extension in Logan County Title Extension regional specialist Member grade Senior member Alma maters Inner Mongolia Normal University, in Hohhot; Beijing Normal University; State University of New York College of Environmental Science and Forestry, in Syracuse; Colorado State University Global She built the AI-Powered Agritourism Chatbot (AgriTourismAI.com), which helps farmers and ranchers launch and run “agritourism” businesses. Agritourism is when farmers open their property to visitors for fun, education, or shopping events. Familiar examples include pick-your-own fruit orchards, lessons on how to grow vegetables, and sales of handmade products. Dong also teaches workshops where she shows farmers and ranchers how they can use AI tools to help grow and manage their business. She says she sees herself as a link between the university and the countryside. “We [extension specialists] act as a bridge,” she says. “We bridge our campus to the rural communities we serve.” Many farmers and ranchers are older, and they typically have no technical training. Often their children and grandchildren have left the farm to work in a city or otherwise aren’t around to teach them about new tools. Without help, the benefits of AI could pass the farmers by. Dong’s workshops give them a way in. Dong was named a finalist in the 2026 GenAI for Good Challenge for her AgriPivot AI Agent. The challenge was organized by IEEE Humanitarian Technologies and the U.N.’s International Telecommunication Union , and her project was selected from 318 teams across 79 countries. She also won the 2026 Award for Innovation from the National Extension Technology Community (NETC) , and both the 2025 national and Western regional Educational Technology Awards from the National Association of Community Development Extension Professionals (NACDEP). She has secured seven competitive grants totaling more than US $250,000 as principal investigator or co-principal investigator, including funding supported by the Department of Agriculture ’s National Institute of Food and Agriculture . An early love of design and problem-solving Dong was born in Beijing. Both her parents are doctors. As a child, she liked drawing new and inventive things. Sketching, she says, lets her picture solutions to problems in her head and put them on paper as practical designs. That habit grew into a way of relating to her surroundings. “I’ve always had a passion to create something tangible that can solve problems in the real world,” she says. She doesn’t credit a single mentor for the direction her life has taken. Instead, she says all her teachers helped lay the groundwork for her career. She attended the Inner Mongolia Normal University , in Hohhot, an institution that trains teachers. She earned two bachelor’s degrees there in 2013—one in geographical science and one in education. She then earned a master’s degree in curriculum and instruction from Beijing Normal University in 2016. That year, she moved to the United States to continue her graduate studies at the State University of New York College of Environmental Science and Forestry , in Syracuse. She earned a master’s degree in environmental biology in 2020. From outreach to extension work After earning her second master’s degree, she joined Paul Smith’s College , in Paul Smiths, N.Y., as an education and outreach coordinator. She managed several national watershed projects to protect rivers, lakes, and aquifers. Watersheds are areas of land from which water drains into bodies of water. She also undertook invasive-species-prevention projects, wrote grants to secure project funding, and designed two educational websites and several outreach publications. One website, Maintain the Chain , helps lake residents, boaters, and visitors from around the world keep invasive species out of the Fulton Chain of Lakes in New York’s Adirondack Park. In 2022, she joined Stewards of the Coast and Redwoods as program manager. The nonprofit, based in Guerneville, Calif., works with California State Parks to protect, restore, and educate the public about the parks along Sonoma County ’s coast and the Russian River area. The region is known for its redwood forests, wineries, and resort towns. She left in 2023 to join the CSU Extension as a regional specialist, a title she still holds. Her employer is part of the Cooperative Extension System , a nationwide network run by land-grant universities , schools founded with federal grants to teach farming and other practical subjects. Extension faculty and staff share what researchers at their universities learn with the citizens of those states. The cooperative system operates on three levels. It is overseen federally by the Department of Agriculture ’s National Institute of Food and Agriculture , managed statewide through land-grant universities, and delivered locally by county offices and Extension agents across more than 3,000 counties. The work goes well beyond farming, Dong says, also covering community and economic development, health initiatives, and the 4-H program , which teaches children hands-on skills in agriculture, science, leadership, and citizenship. Extension faculty members’ performance is judged on their research, teaching, and service to the community, Dong says—similar to the way professors in academia are evaluated. The difference, she says, is the audience: Professors teach students; most extension specialists teach adults, including farmers, ranchers, and community leaders. The setting is different, too. Dong doesn’t commute from the campus to the countryside; she lives and works in it. Her office is in Sterling, a small rural town. But her projects serve the whole state, and many of the people she helps live one to four hours’ drive away. So, most of her work with farmers and ranchers happens by email, phone, and virtual meetings. County fairs, farmers markets, and agricultural events give her chances to meet large groups of them in person. She can’t just hand Colorado residents research findings and expect them to figure out the information they need, she says. “We need to translate that research into something more practical, and easier to use, that farmers and ranchers can understand immediately,” she says. Dong also focuses not on only on whether people use AI, but also on how they use it. In 2026, she and Paul Hill from Utah State University Extension published “From Access to Governance: Generative AI Literacy for Extension Professionals and Small Businesses, and a Governance-Aware Design Framework” in the journal AI . The paper offers a framework for helping Extension professionals and small businesses adopt generative AI responsibly. How her AI chatbot helps farmers and ranchers In 2025, Dong earned a third master’s degree , in artificial intelligence and machine learning, from CSU Global . She immediately put those skills to work on agritourism, she says. She built the chatbot in Python , a popular programming language . It answers typed questions, and its user interface looks much like ChatGPT ’s, but it works differently. Under the hood, it uses retrieval-augmented generation, a technique that has the AI look up information in a set of trusted documents before it answers. Dong curated that collection from Extension publications, so the chatbot’s answers rest on authoritative sources and are less likely to be made up. She presented the project at NeurIPS 2025 (Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems). The code is openly available on GitHub, so other Extension offices can adapt it. The bot runs in a web browser rather than as a phone app. Many farmers she works with don’t own a smartphone, Dong says, but nearly all have a computer, tablet, or other gadget that can connect to a website. The bot works on any of them, with no app to download. Extension specialists “act as a bridge. We bridge our campus to the rural communities we serve.” Farmers often ask the bot how to attract visitors and how to write a business plan. A farmer thinking about opening a corn maze, for example, can ask how to price admission, what kind of insurance to carry, and which permits to get. The bot also gives advice on managing risk. One of her test sites was Prairie Ridge Buffalo Ranch , in eastern Colorado. Dong documented how the ranch put AI to work in a peer-reviewed case study, “Revolutionizing Agritourism with AI and Machine Learning: A Case Study of Prairie Ridge Buffalo Ranch in Colorado,” published in 2025 in CABI Tourism Cases . Surveys and interviews she conducted with other users showed that people find it’s easy to use the bot, learn from it, and act on its advice, she says. She is preparing the full results for publication. Her work extends beyond agritourism. In 2026, she contributed an AI assistant to Project Pythia, an open-science program funded by the U.S. National Science Foundation and led by the National Center for Atmospheric Research (NCAR) . The AI assistant turns raw airport weather report data into plain-language guidance for farmers and other non-technical users, and it tells users when data is missing rather than guessing. She also teaches workshops on AI tools such as ChatGPT, Claude , and Gemini . She has taught her workshop 20 times to more than 200 entrepreneurs and business owners, who came from 32 Colorado counties. In follow-up surveys, 90 percent of participants reported trying at least one new AI task in their business. Some of the workshops take place at a community center run by the Logan County Economic Development Corp ., in Sterling. She has also co-hosted the workshops with the Rural Community Assistance Corp ., Colorado Startup Week , and Boulder Startup Week . And she occasionally presents them as webinars, so people don’t have to travel. Her outreach has taught her that many farmers are eager to try new tools , she says. She shows them how simple her chatbot is to use. She also offers advice to high school students drawn to the field. Extension specialists each have a specialty, such as livestock, natural resources, food systems, or 4-H. Students should pick one based on their passion, she says. Land-grant universities offer related programs at the bachelor’s and master’s levels. For graduate students, she adds, Extension offers a third career path beyond academia and industry: “You apply advanced skills directly to the communities that need them.” How IEEE membership supports her career Dong joined IEEE in 2025 and soon was elevated to senior member. Her professional home is the IEEE Society on Social Implications of Technology . She also serves as vice treasurer of the IEEE Denver Section’s Young Professionals group . IEEE supports all three parts of her job, she says. For research, she presented “Entrepreneur AI Agent: Empowering Small Businesses and Bridging the Digital Divide through Context-Aware Generative AI” at the 2026 IEEE Global Humanitarian Technology Conference (GHTC). For teaching, she has offered to bring her AI workshop to Denver Section members and local entrepreneurs. For service, she reviews papers for IEEE conferences. IEEE conferences matter most to her, she says: “Through them, I can present my research and network with other researchers in the field.” She attended the IEEE World Forum on Public Safety Technology in Boulder, Colo., in September 2026. The event, she says, opened her eyes to many new projects underway across IEEE. Still, she says, her work always points back to the farms and ranches of eastern Colorado. Its people are curious, she says, but they can’t make the leap to new technology alone. “They really need this kind of a bridge,” she says.

summary: 香港通过新工业园和贸易指南推动模块化建设中国劳工布告栏 星期日, 2026 年 11 月 22 日 · 香港 香港和中国劳工英文新闻 香港推动新工业园的模块化建筑，贸易指南 香港发展局局长表示，超过 150 个项目已采用模块化建筑 (MiC)。政府正在新界北部预留30公顷土地作为先进建筑工业园，并启动了制造商认证计划和跨境贸易 香港发展局局长叶国雄
content:
香港通过新工业园和贸易指南推动模块化建设中国劳工公告栏
星期日, 22 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港及中国劳工新闻（英文）
香港通过新工业园和贸易指南推动模块化建设
香港发展局局长表示，模块化建筑（MiC）已被超过 150 个项目采用。政府正在新界北部预留30公顷土地兴建先进建筑工业园，并推出制造商认证计划和跨境贸易
香港发展局局长叶国雄表示，政府正在推动高效建筑，其中模块化集成建筑（MiC）是过去十年最引人注目的成就之一。叶说，超过150个公私营项目已采用MiC，涵盖员工宿舍、公共房屋、私人住宅及大学宿舍。
叶在模块化建筑国际会议开幕礼上表示，政府已宣布计划在新界北部预留30公顷土地兴建大型先进建筑工业园。该园区旨在在香港及其他地区推广高端建筑技术。
叶表示，发展局已实施一系列措施加强MiC供应链。其中包括启动MiC制造商认证计划、与内地当局合作发布《粤港MiC模块化建筑跨境贸易指南》以及与广东省住房和城乡建设厅签署合作协议。
该协议旨在共同提升两地工程建设标准，通过协同工作机制，协调指导粤港澳大湾区建设标准制定。
发展局在社交媒体上表示，叶先生亦见证香港大学在发展局及香港建筑科技学会的支持下，发布首个MiC标准及MiC指南。叶先生称该出版物为制定大湾区 MiC 标准奠定了基础。

Hong Kong pushes modular construction with new industry park, trade guide | China Labour Bulletin Board
Sunday, 22 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Hong Kong pushes modular construction with new industry park, trade guide
Hong Kong's Development Bureau chief says modular construction (MiC) has been adopted by over 150 projects. The government is reserving 30 hectares in the Northern New Territories for an advanced construction industry park, and has launched a manufacturer accreditation scheme and a cross-border trad
Hong Kong's Development Bureau chief Arion Ip said the government is pushing efficient construction, with modular integrated construction (MiC) one of the most notable achievements of the past decade. More than 150 public and private projects have adopted MiC, covering staff quarters, public housing, private homes and university dormitories, Ip said.
Speaking at the opening ceremony of the Modular Building International Conference, Ip said the government has announced plans to reserve 30 hectares of land in the Northern New Territories for a large-scale advanced construction industry park. The park aims to promote high-end construction technology in Hong Kong and beyond.
Ip said the Development Bureau has implemented a series of measures to strengthen the MiC supply chain. These include launching a MiC manufacturer accreditation scheme, publishing the Guangdong-Hong Kong MiC Modular Building Cross-Border Trade Guide in collaboration with mainland authorities, and signing a cooperation agreement with the Guangdong Provincial Department of Housing and Urban-Rural Development.
The agreement aims to jointly raise engineering and construction standards in both places and, through a collaborative working mechanism, coordinate and guide the setting of construction standards for the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macau Greater Bay Area.
The Development Bureau said on social media that Ip also witnessed the University of Hong Kong release the first MiC standard and MiC guide, supported by the bureau and the Hong Kong Institute of Building Technology. Ip described the publication as laying the foundation for setting Greater Bay Area MiC standards.

title: China, US, Russia issue ‘Declaration toward Peace’ after first summit
zh_title: 中美俄首次峰会后发表《和平宣言》
summary: 中国、美国和俄罗斯领导人举行史无前例的峰会后于周四发表了《和平宣言》，提出了改革联合国和控制国际刑事法院的共同目标。 2026 年 11 月 19 日，在中国南部广东省深圳举行的亚太经合组织 (APEC) 峰会期间，俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京、中国国家主席习近平和美国总统唐纳德·特朗普抵达麒麟山庄参加三方会议时合影留念。照片：Vyacheslav Prokofyev/法新社。习近平、唐纳德·特鲁
content:
中国、美国和俄罗斯领导人举行史无前例的峰会后于周四发表了《和平宣言》，提出了改革联合国和控制国际刑事法院的共同目标。 2026 年 11 月 19 日，在中国南部广东省深圳举行的亚太经合组织 (APEC) 峰会期间，俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京、中国国家主席习近平和美国总统唐纳德·特朗普抵达麒麟山庄参加三方会议时合影留念。照片：Vyacheslav Prokofyev/法新社。习近平、特朗普和普京在中国会晤的背景复杂，俄罗斯在乌克兰的攻势持续多年，特朗普在中东陷入困境，而崛起的中国则希望加强在东亚的影响力。白宫版本的声明称，“三位国家元首就当前国际形势深入交换了意见，致力于维护战略稳定和国际安全。” “我们讨论了民主问题。什么是民主？它是什么？这是某些圈子联合起来的自由秩序，现在仍在试图强加给全世界，”普京在南方城市深圳举行的新闻发布会上说。三人围坐在一张深色的大圆桌前，围绕从核武器到乌克兰战争等重大话题发表了开场白，圆桌中央摆放着粉红色的花朵。
麒麟山庄的闭门讨论在1小时20分钟后结束。特朗普称领导人正在“创造历史”，普京则称他们写下了“外交史上新的一页”。习近平表示，“三个国家在维护世界和平方面有着共同的观点”。在返回华盛顿的途中，特朗普召集了一次欧洲领导人会议，讨论乌克兰问题并向他们通报三方峰会的最新情况。 2026 年 2 月，布鲁塞尔欧盟委员会总部前悬挂着乌克兰和欧盟旗帜。照片：欧盟委员会。并非所有欧洲领导人都对此印象深刻：德国总理弗里德里希·梅尔茨称特朗普-习近平-普京会谈是一次“合影”，法国总统埃马纽埃尔·马克龙表示，这不会“导致世界重组”。特朗普表示，他将于周五举行新闻发布会，介绍他“伟大且影响深远的中国之行”。国际刑事法院、联合国和石油在联合声明中，特朗普、习近平和普京“认识到国家同意和尊重国家官员豁免权的原则至关重要，并同意国际刑事法院和其他类似机构不得滥用管辖权”。普京受到国际刑事法院逮捕令的制裁，而特朗普政府则誓言要“一砖一瓦”解散该法院。国际刑事法院。资料照片：维基共享资源。
领导人表示，他们“致力于改革联合国，使联合国能够更有效地应对全球挑战，履行其国际和平与安全的基本使命”。联合声明称，各国计划增加成品油供应和生产，并重申“稳定能源流动”的重要性。这次峰会引发了人们的担忧，担心这三人想要将全球划分为势力范围，例如通过做出影响乌克兰而不是基辅或欧洲的决定。但特朗普表示，他希望“欧洲站在他一边”就乌克兰问题达成协议

【原文 English Original】
China, the United States and Russia issued a “Declaration toward Peace” on Thursday after their leaders held an unprecedented summit, laying out common ambitions to overhaul the UN and keep the International Criminal Court in check. Russia’s President Vladimir Putin, China’s President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump pose for photos as they arrive for a trilateral meeting at Kylin Villa on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Summit in Shenzhen, in China’s southern Guangdong province, on November 19, 2026. Photo: Vyacheslav Prokofyev/AFP. Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin met in China against a complex backdrop, with Russia’s years-long offensive in Ukraine grinding on, Trump bogged down in the Middle East and an ascendant China looking to strengthen its hand in East Asia. “The three heads of state had an in-depth exchange of views on the current international situation and committed to maintaining strategic stability and international security,” a White House version of the statement said. “We discussed the question of democracy. And what is democracy? It’s what? It’s the liberal order that certain circles put together and still now are trying to impose on the whole world,” Putin told a news conference in the southern city of Shenzhen. The three men made opening remarks touching on weighty topics from nuclear weapons to the war in Ukraine as they met around a large, dark round table with a pink flower arrangement at its centre. The discussion behind closed doors in Kylin Villa ended after an hour and 20 minutes. Trump said the leaders were “making history”, while Putin said they wrote a new “page in the history of diplomacy”. “The three countries share a common perspective on safeguarding world peace,” Xi said. On his way home to Washington, Trump called into a meeting of European leaders to discuss Ukraine and update them on his three-way summit. Ukrainian and European Union flags in front of the European Commission headquarters in Brussels in February 2026. Photo: European Commission. Not all of those European leaders were impressed: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz called the Trump-Xi-Putin talks a “photo op”, and French President Emmanuel Macron said it would not “lead to a reorganisation of the world”. Trump said he would give a press conference on Friday about his “Great and Highly Consequential Trip” to China. ICC, UN and oil In their joint statement, Trump, Xi and Putin “recognised that the principle of state consent and respect for immunities of State officials are of paramount importance, and concurred that the International Criminal Court and other similar bodies must not abuse their jurisdiction”. Putin is subject to an ICC arrest warrant, while Trump’s administration has vowed to dismantle the court “brick by brick”. International Criminal Court. File photo: Wikicommons. The leaders said they were “committed to reform the UN so that the UN can respond more effectively to global challenges and conform to its fundamental mission of international peace and security”. The joint statement said the countries plan to boost supply and production of refined petroleum products, and reaffirmed the importance of “stable energy flows”. The summit stoked fears that the three men want to divide the globe into spheres of influence , for example by making decisions impacting Ukraine over the heads of Kyiv or Europe. But Trump said he wanted to make a deal on Ukraine “with Europe by his side”, accourding to special US envoy Jared Kushner. ‘Reducing nuclear risks’ Earlier Thursday, Trump and Putin held a meeting — their first since August 2025 — with the 80-year-old US president calling the Russian his “friend”. Putin responded in English: “Nice to meet you.” Trump and Xi then came together — their third time this year — for one-on-one discussions, with the US leader highlighting a “very special relationship”. Putin, 74, and Xi, 73, held talks on Wednesday — their 50th meeting, the Chinese president said. Beijing, Washington and Moscow previously gave different accounts of the agenda for the three-way meeting on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, a forum of 21 economies around the Pacific Rim. Washington initially signalled that Ukraine was off the table, before Trump said the war would feature. Xi does not view the conflict as China’s problem to solve. Washington had also flagged up the Iran war and nuclear disarmament as topics of discussion, after a US-Russia bilateral treaty on atomic weapons expired in February. Beijing has long maintained that the United States and Russia must reduce their giant nuclear arsenals before it agrees to talks on its smaller stockpile. China’s nuclear arsenal. File Photo: CCTV screenshot. The final statement said that the countries would “conduct a dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing the proliferation of nuclear weapons.” ‘Cheap violin’ Breaking with decades of diplomatic protocol, Xi met Trump at the airport, with the men briefly hugging before a red-carpet greeting complete with cheering children and a flyover. Critics warned that the optics from the meeting would be damaging for the US president — but a fillip to Xi and Putin. The meeting “gives Putin a platform to legitimise his war of aggression over Ukraine with seemingly little repercussions”, said Lyle Morris at the Asia Society Policy Institute. “Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin are playing Donald Trump like a cheap violin,” Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer said.

content:
AEON信用报告在香港未经授权的系统访问|中国劳工公告栏
星期日, 22 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港及中国劳工新闻（英文）
AEON信用报告在香港未经授权的系统访问
永旺信贷金融服务（亚洲）表示，其系统在未经授权的情况下被访问。尚未发现数据滥用的证据，并且已启动独立的网络安全调查。
永旺信贷财务（亚洲）有限公司在其网站上发布的“重要通知”中表示，该公司报告称其计算机系统遭到未经授权的访问。该公司表示，现阶段没有证据表明任何相关数据被不当使用。
该公司表示，非常严肃地对待这一事件，并将继续密切关注事态发展，防止再次发生。它补充说，发现漏洞后立即采取行动，以遏制其影响并加强系统安全。
AEON 已委托独立第三方网络安全和数字取证专家协助调查该事件并评估潜在后果。该公司敦促客户保持警惕，并表示将分别通知受影响的客户为保护其利益而采取的措施。
该通知没有具体说明违规事件发生的时间、可能影响的客户数量或可能访问的数据类型。调查正在进行中。
